P2800.d: P2800 is the general circuit code for the second signal path that tells the modules which selector position (P, R, N, D, L) is engaged. It applies when that signal is unusable without a clear low, high or frequency pattern.
s: Wrench lamp or MIL on, gear display missing or wrong
Engine does not start in Park or Neutral
Trouble selecting a drive position
c: Water entry or corrosion in connectors along the sensor circuit
Chafed or broken wiring between sensor and module
Invalid gear position message from another module over CAN

P2801.d: Here the B signal of the range sensor is electrically present but its content does not make sense. On sensors with a pulse-width output, Ford checks the carrier frequency: its 2024 summary sets P2801 (UDS P2800_38) on the 6R80, 6R140, 10R60 and 10R80 automatics when the frequency leaves 125 Hz plus or minus 25 Hz, while the 2012 summary applies the same test to the 250 Hz signal of the DPS6 dual-clutch box.
s: Warning lamp with shift quality or gear display issues
Transmission uses a fixed substitute range strategy
c: Range sensor electronics producing a wrong signal frequency
Damaged or loose pins at the transmission connector
Sensor shifted on its shaft so the angles disagree

P2802.d: P2802 means the B signal of the range sensor sits too low, usually a ground short or a duty cycle collapsing toward zero. GM's tables for 2020 and 2025 place the check in the engine module, which reads internal range sensor B on its own wire: a circuit impedance under 0.5 ohm to ground for 0.5 s within a one-second window sets the code as Type A, MIL in the first trip.
s: MIL or wrench lamp on
No start in Park, missing gear indication
Stop-start or shift functions restricted
c: Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in a connector of the circuit
Range sensor output stage failed low

P2803.d: P2803 is stored when the output of range sensor B reads too high, which typically points to an open circuit or a short to supply voltage. In GM's 2020 and 2025 tables the engine module watches its own range sensor input for this: either under 0.5 ohm to the voltage source or above 200 kilohms to ground for 0.5 s sets a Type A fault.
s: MIL on, often with transmission temperature codes
Shift system warning in the instrument cluster
Wrong or missing gear display
c: Open signal circuit or pushed-out connector pin
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source
Module calibration misreading the signal, fixed by software

P2804.d: P2804 points to a B signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. Ford is the main user: its 2024 OBD summary books it as the general electrical fault of TRS B (UDS P2800_01), checked continuously, with up to 30 s allowed for pattern recognition and 2 s for analog faults.
s: MIL comes and goes, often with several transmission codes
Gear display flickers
Occasional shift system warning
c: Connector not fully seated or pin pushed back
Harness chafing that opens the circuit under vibration
Worn contacts or electronics inside the range sensor

P2805.d: Both range sensor signals are valid on their own, yet they do not agree. Many designs output two complementary pulse-width signals whose duty cycles must add up to 100 %.
s: MIL and gearbox warning on
Engine will not start or selector position not accepted
Substitute gear or limp operation
c: Range sensor with one drifting output
Added resistance or poor ground in one of the two signal paths
Fault in the reading control module

P2806.d: P2806 says that the selector position reported by the range sensor and the actual mechanical position of the gearbox do not line up. Ford is the only public user found.
s: Wrench lamp, gear display differs from lever position
Vehicle may roll in Park
Start refused in Park or Neutral
c: Range sensor not aligned correctly after transmission work
Stretched selector cable or worn linkage
Park pawl or park motor mechanism damaged

P2807.d: P2807 is the umbrella code for pressure control solenoid G; the fault type follows in the extra byte. Which hydraulic function G controls is set by each maker.
s: MIL on with harsh or delayed shifts
Whine noise from the transmission
Reduced power or limp mode
c: Debris or wear particles jamming the valve
Solenoid G worn or electrically weak

P2808.d: P2808 means valve G does not deliver the pressure or effect it is commanded to give. GM documents two very different applications.
s: MIL on, engine speed higher than expected at cruise
Higher fuel consumption and transmission heat
Limited-slip function inactive on Corvette
c: Valve G stuck by contamination so pressure stays low
Worn converter clutch lining that slips despite pressure
Low fluid level or internal leak in the circuit

P2809.d: P2809 is the reverse case: valve G keeps acting although it should have released. On GM's 2016 eight-speed automatics, where G operates the converter lockup clutch, the converter shows almost no slip, between minus 50 and plus 30 rpm, while the clutch is commanded off; after 1.5 s and six fail counts the controller stores the code, with the MIL lit in the first trip.
s: Engine stalls or shudders when coming to a stop
MIL on
Differential stays locked on Corvette, tyre scrub in tight turns
c: Valve G held open by debris

P280A.d: P280A means the module holds no valid learned reference for range sensor A, so it cannot translate the raw signal into a reliable selector position. This is typical after replacing the sensor, the gearbox or the control module, after a software update, or when a learn run was aborted.
s: Warning lamp right after a repair or update
Engine does not start or gear display missing
c: Learn procedure skipped after replacing sensor, gearbox or module
Learn run aborted, for example by low battery voltage
Learned values cleared by a software update
Sensor signal outside the learnable window

P280B.d: P280B flags missing or invalid adaptation values for the second range sensor signal. Where a design reads A and B in different modules, as GM does with sensor A in the TCM and sensor B in the engine module, a replaced or reprogrammed engine controller can lose the B reference while A is still learned.
s: Warning lamp after module replacement
Gear position checks disabled, possible start refusal
c: Module reading sensor B replaced or reprogrammed without learn
Open circuit faults on sensor B preventing the learn

P2810.d: P2810 is a collective electrical code for solenoid G: the control unit sees a fault in coil or wiring but does not split it into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents P2810 publicly.
s: MIL on and harsh shifts
Transmission in default pressure or limp mode
c: Coil of solenoid G open or shorted internally
Damaged internal harness or lead frame
Faulty output stage in the control module

P2811.d: With P2811 the module records that valve G misbehaved only for moments, electrically or in effect, and then recovered. No maker publishes a description of this exact code.
s: Occasional harsh shift, then normal again
MIL that comes and goes
c: Loose terminal or fretting corrosion in the gearbox connector
Intermittent contact inside the valve body solenoid assembly
Coil that fails only when hot

P2812.d: P2812 signals an open control circuit of solenoid G. GM uses it widely: on the 2016 eight-speed (TCC valve) the hardware open flag must stand for 0.3 s of 0.5 s, one trip; the 2020 table, now with the ten-speed line pressure valve as well, asks for 0.6 s of 0.65 s and rates it Type B; on the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box it is the limited-slip valve, detected by a driver chip test with the output off and confirmed af
s: Check engine light on
Harsh shifts on line pressure designs
No converter lockup or limited-slip function
c: Open coil in solenoid G or in the valve body assembly
Open terminal or corroded pin in the transmission connector
Broken wire between module and solenoid
Faulty output driver in the control module

P2813.d: On paper P2813 is a plausibility fault in the control circuit of solenoid G, but its main real-world use is hydraulic. Nissan-built CVTs label it as the select solenoid, which applies the forward and reverse clutches.
s: Strong shock when selecting D or R
Slow start and weak acceleration
MIL after the second trip
c: Select solenoid valve sticking in the valve body
CVT wear with belt slip or clutch damage
Added resistance in the solenoid circuit

P2814.d: P2814 reports that the drive line of solenoid G is pulled toward ground, typically a chafed wire or a coil shorted to ground. GM's 2020 tables name G as the line pressure valve on nine- and ten-speed boxes and the converter clutch valve on the eight-speed; a resistance of about 0.5 ohm to ground, present for 0.3 s out of a 0.5 s sample, sets a Type A fault.
s: MIL or transmission warning on, often with a fault message
Firm shifts because line pressure falls back to a fixed value
Converter clutch no longer locks up (eight-speed applications)
Limited-slip differential inactive on dual-clutch Corvettes
c: Solenoid G control wire chafed through to ground in the gearbox harness
Solenoid G coil with internal short to its housing
Fault inside the valve body assembly (GM 10-speed, PIP5799)
Damaged output stage in the transmission control module

P2815.d: P2815 is the opposite electrical case: the driver of solenoid G sees battery voltage where the load should pull the pin down. In GM's 2016 eight-speed table, where G is the converter clutch pressure valve, the flag must stand for 0.3 s of a 0.5 s window and one trip is enough.
s: MIL lit and transmission in a substitute program
Harsh engagement or missing converter lockup
Code may appear only after the next engine start (shutdown test)
c: Control wire of solenoid G touching a supply voltage wire
Solenoid coil with shorted turns drawing too much current
Two solenoid outputs shorted together inside the harness or valve body
Faulty driver stage in the transmission module

P2816.d: P2816 is the general code for pressure control solenoid H; a fault type byte usually narrows it down. The valve H stands for depends on the maker.
s: MIL on, sometimes reduced engine power
Harsh or erratic shifts
Whining noise from the transmission
c: Internal transmission damage leaving debris in the hydraulics (Toyota eight-speed)
Valve H sticking in its bore

P2817.d: P2817 means valve H fails to produce the effect it is commanded to give. On GM nine- and ten-speed automatics H is the converter clutch valve: too much slip in lock mode (130 rpm) or a large slip error in controlled mode, counted three times, sets a Type A fault.
s: MIL on or flashing D indicator
Converter clutch slips, engine speed higher than usual at cruise
Increased fuel consumption
c: Valve H stuck or hydraulically unable to apply
Damaged turbine shaft seal letting converter clutch pressure escape (GM 8T65)
Misjudged pressure signal in older control software (Honda CVT)

P2818.d: P2818 reports that valve H stays effective when it should be released. In GM's eight-speed table for the 8L90, H is the default valve: in Park at 400-900 rpm, with fluid between 0 and 40 °C and a converter clutch test pressure of 600 kPa, slip of 6 rpm or less for 0.5 s counts as a fail, and the MIL follows after two trips.
s: Engine stalls when coming to a stop or when D or R is selected
Firm upshifts or downshifts, shudder
MIL on, code may set only at low fluid temperature
c: Valve in the valve body sticking in the applied position
Internal transmission fault that persists when cold (PI1405)

P2819.d: P2819 is a collective electrical code for solenoid H: the module knows that coil or wiring is faulty but does not say whether the circuit is open or shorted. Mercedes-Benz uses it on the 8G-DCT dual-clutch gearbox (transmission 724.1 in the A-Class, CLA and GLA/GLB families): P281900, an electrical fault of pressure regulating valve 8, is one of the codes its guided diagnosis tool in XENTRY handles, alongside P281600
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Limp-home mode with restricted gears
Jerky starts or rough shifts
c: Coil of valve H open or shorted
Poor contact between valve and mechatronic or module board

P281A.d: P281A marks a fault at valve H that comes and goes, either electrically or in its hydraulic effect. There is no public manufacturer description of P281A.
s: Occasional harsh or delayed shift
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short spells of limp-home mode
c: Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector
Coil of valve H failing only at operating temperature
Cracked solder joint in an integrated mechatronic unit

P281B.d: P281B stands for an open control circuit of solenoid H. GM's 2020 tables apply it to the converter clutch valve of nine- and ten-speed automatics and to the T93 eight-speed default valve; an impedance of about 200 kilohm, seen for 0.3 s of 0.5 s, sets a Type A fault in one trip.
s: MIL on after one trip
No converter clutch lockup, higher engine speed at cruise
Limited-slip differential disabled (Corvette dual-clutch)
c: Terminal pushed back or loose in the connector
Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness

P281C.d: P281C is meant for a circuit of solenoid H that is electrically intact but does not behave plausibly, for example when the measured current fails to follow the commanded value. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only demands functional monitoring of output circuits.
s: MIL or transmission warning on
Shift quality varies from drive to drive
Possible substitute program
c: Coil resistance of valve H outside specification
Corroded or loose contacts raising circuit resistance
Unstable supply voltage to the solenoid driver

P281D.d: P281D signals that the control line of solenoid H is shorted to ground. In GM's 2016 eight-speed table H is the on/off default valve; the low flag must persist for 0.3 s within 0.5 s and one trip lights the MIL.
s: MIL on after a single trip
Transmission in default gear or fixed pressure mode
Converter lockup or differential lock unavailable
c: Control wire of solenoid H shorted to ground
Open default valve circuit reported as low (GM T87a eight-speed)
Coil insulation failure inside solenoid H

P281E.d: P281E sets when the line to solenoid H carries supply voltage where the module expects the load to pull it down. GM's 2020 tables cover the converter clutch valve on nine- and ten-speed automatics and the default valve on the eight-speed with the same timing as the low code: 0.3 s within 0.5 s, Type A, one trip.
s: MIL on, possibly right after starting
Converter clutch or differential lock function lost
Firm shifts in a substitute program
c: Control wire of solenoid H shorted to a voltage source
Moisture in the transmission connector bridging pins
Short between solenoid H and a neighbouring output

P281F.d: P281F is the umbrella code for pressure control solenoid J; usually a failure-type byte narrows it down, or the module stores one of the specific codes P2820 to P2827 instead. Which valve carries the letter J is up to each manufacturer.
s: Harsh or delayed gear changes
Transmission warning message or MIL
Limited gears or emergency mode
c: Valve J sticking due to abrasion particles in the fluid
Fault inside the mechatronic unit or valve body
Coil or connector fault at valve J

P2820.d: P2820 says valve J, though electrically sound, fails to deliver its hydraulic effect when commanded. On GM ten-speed automatics J is the default disable valve; if it sticks off, the box drops into its hydraulic limp gear (2nd or 7th) while another gear is requested.
s: Transmission suddenly holds 2nd or 7th gear
Binding or jerky drive when the wrong clutches engage
Vehicle will not leave Park on dual-clutch models
MIL on
c: Casting debris or dirt blocking valve J or its passages
Restricted orifice in a spacer plate
Outdated control logic that misjudges the valve (Toyota CVT)
Internal transmission damage requiring a replacement unit

P2821.d: P2821 is the mirror image of P2820: valve J keeps acting after the module has released it. GM bulletin PIP5557 (revisions up to C) concerns 2018 Cruze, Equinox, Malibu and Traverse with nine-speed automatics (RPO M3D, M3E, M3H, M3U, M3V) that stay in second gear and will not pass about 30 mph.
s: Stuck in second gear, no upshift
Top speed limited to about 50 km/h
Park lock does not engage as expected
MIL on
c: Blocked orifice in the valve body spacer plate
Valve J or its spool stuck in the applied position
TCM software requiring the update released with the repair
Park lock piston or latching valve not draining (dual-clutch)

P2822.d: P2822 gathers electrical faults of solenoid J without saying whether the circuit is open or shorted; a failure-type byte adds that detail. Mercedes-Benz uses the code on two gearboxes, and in both J is pressure regulating valve 9.
s: Transmission warning or MIL
Emergency mode with fixed gear
Code present on a new car without driveability complaint
c: Short to positive in the valve J circuit
Signal timing when leaving transport mode on new vehicles (Mercedes 9G-Tronic)
Open or shorted coil of valve J
Corrosion or loose pins at the transmission connector

P2823.d: P2823 is reserved for a fault at valve J that appears and disappears, either in its wiring or in its hydraulic action. No manufacturer publishes a description of this code.
s: Occasional rough or unexpected shift
Warning that comes and goes
Sometimes delayed park lock response
c: Loose or spread pin at the transmission connector
Coil that drops out only when hot
Valve J sticking now and then due to contaminated fluid

P2824.d: P2824 reports an open in the control line of solenoid J. GM's 2016 table for T87 eight-speed controllers uses J for the on/off boost valve of clutch 2 and flags the code in one trip once the fault persists 0.3 s within a half-second sample.
s: Hydraulic limp gear or no shifting
Park lock cannot be operated (dual-clutch models)
MIL on after one or two trips
c: Broken wire between TCM and valve J
Terminal pushed back or not latched in the connector
Faulty output driver in the TCM

P2825.d: P2825 would flag a J control circuit that is intact but behaves implausibly, for example a current that does not track the duty cycle the module commands. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only requires functional checks of output circuits in general terms.
s: Shift quality varies
MIL or transmission warning
c: Coil resistance out of specification when hot
Sluggish valve J changing the electrical load

P2826.d: P2826 indicates that the line to solenoid J is pulled to ground. GM's 2020 tables name three uses for J: the clutch select valve of the nine-speed, the default disable valve of the ten-speed and the boost valve of the eight-speed.
s: Limp gear or loss of boost pressure
Park lock fault message (dual-clutch models)
MIL on
c: Control wire shorted to ground through chafed insulation
Coil of valve J shorted to its housing
Open J circuit reported as low on GM T87a controllers

P2827.d: P2827 sets when the J control line shows supply voltage although the load ought to pull it low. In GM's 2020 tables it covers the nine-speed clutch valve, the ten-speed default disable valve and the eight-speed boost valve, using the same 0.3-of-0.5 s window and Type A rating as the low code.
s: Limp gear or blocked park lock function
Code returns right after a restart
MIL on
c: Control wire shorted to a supply line
Short to a neighbouring solenoid output
Shorted coil turns lowering the load

P2828.d: P2828 serves as the catch-all code for solenoid K and is normally refined by a failure-type byte or replaced by one of P2829 to P2830. Mercedes-Benz is the maker found to name it directly: on the 8G-DCT dual-clutch gearbox of model series 118, 177 and 247, P282800 denotes a malfunction of pressure regulating valve 10 and P282B00 an electrical fault of the same valve.
s: Rough shifting or missing gears
Transmission warning or MIL
Emergency mode
c: Valve K sticking because of contaminated fluid
Fault in the mechatronic unit carrying valve K

P2829.d: P2829 means valve K remains hydraulically inactive although it is commanded on. In GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch transmission K is the selector pilot valve, which steers the selector spool of the shift-rod hydraulics.
s: Some gears unavailable
Hesitation or failed gear preselection
MIL on
c: Selector pilot valve stuck in the off position
Abrasion particles in the transmission fluid
Selector spool itself stuck (same symptom, different part)

P282A.d: P282A reports the reverse of P2829: K holds the selector mechanism in its pressurized state after being switched off. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software uses the same synchronizer integrity routine, this time with a test case whose selector target is hydraulic off.
s: Gears locked out or limp mode
Clunk or unexpected rod movement during shifts
MIL on
c: Selector pilot valve stuck in the applied position
Worn valve bore causing internal leakage

P282B.d: P282B covers electrical faults at solenoid K when the module does not break them down into open, low or high. Mercedes-Benz uses P282B00 on the 8G-DCT (transmission 724.1) for an electrical fault of pressure regulating valve 10; its 2025 information LI27.00-P-077141 includes the code among those the IPR guided routine analyses before parts are replaced, while P282800 stands for a functional fault of that valve.
s: Rough clutch engagement
Transmission warning or MIL
Emergency mode
c: Broken coil winding in valve K
Damaged internal conductor in the mechatronic unit

P282C.d: P282C is intended for an intermittent problem at solenoid K. No manufacturer publishes a description; CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requires monitoring of transmission actuators without prescribing a separate code for sporadic faults.
s: Occasional failed gear preselection
Warning that disappears after restart
c: Weak pin tension or unlatched connector
Heat-related dropout of the coil or internal lead

P282D.d: P282D marks an open control circuit of solenoid K. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch software applies it to the selector pilot valve.
s: Gears on one shaft unavailable
MIL on immediately
Limp mode
c: Broken wire to the selector pilot valve
Terminal pushed back in the connector

P282E.d: P282E is meant for a solenoid K control circuit whose behaviour strays from what the TCM expects although there is no clean open or short. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 states the monitoring duty only in general form.
s: Uneven gear preselection
MIL or transmission warning
c: Poor ground or supply to the driver stage
Weak output stage in the TCM

P282F.d: P282F reports a ground fault on the control line of solenoid K. On the 2023 Corvette, GM checks the selector pilot valve while its low-side output is switched on; the TCM compares the voltage at the sense pin with a lower limit of about 1.7 V, and a reading below it points to a ground short.
s: Gears on one clutch shaft blocked
MIL on in the same trip
Limp mode
c: Control wire to valve K shorted to ground
Damaged insulation inside the transmission harness
Coil of valve K shorted to ground internally

P2830.d: P2830 is set when the K control line carries voltage where the switched-on low-side driver should pull it down. GM applies it to the selector pilot valve of the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch box with a limit that climbs as supply voltage increases, from about 0.7 V below 11.5 V to 1.1 V above 15.5 V, confirmed after 100 ms.
s: Gear preselection fails, limp mode
Code back immediately after restart
MIL on
c: Control wire shorted to a supply line
Short to an adjacent solenoid output

P2831.d: P2831 is the general circuit code for the position signal of shift fork A in automated manual and dual-clutch gearboxes. How makers fill it varies widely.
s: Transmission warning, gear display may flash
Odd gears unavailable or limp-home mode
Delayed engagement or no drive when starting off
c: Shift fork A position sensor electrically defective
Fault in the module's motor current controller (Ford DPS6)
Poor contact at the sensor or module connector

P2832.d: P2832 means the fork A position reading is electrically valid but disagrees with what the gearbox is doing. GM's 2023 table for the Corvette dual-clutch box runs this as a consistency check on rod 1: when clutch shaft and output speeds prove a gear is engaged with over 600 N applied, yet the sensor sits more than 1100 µm away from the learned engaged position, a Type A fault follows a confirmation time; a matching te
s: Gear on the odd shaft not engaged or dropped
Clunks or long pauses during shifts
Limp-home mode with warning lamp
c: Sensor magnet or mounting shifted on the shift rod
Learned fork positions no longer valid after repair or wear
Shift rod, fork or drum binding mechanically

P2833.d: P2833 reports a fork A position signal stuck at the low end. On the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox the rod 1 sensor sends a pulse-width signal; GM's 2023 table sets the code when no pulses arrive and the pin stays under 2.0 V, or when the duty cycle drops below 8 %, each confirmed for 150 ms, with the 5 V sensor supply in range and rated Type A.
s: Warning lamp and limp-home mode
Gears of one shaft locked out
Car may only pull away in a fallback gear
c: Signal wire of the fork A sensor shorted to ground
Open signal line letting the input float low

P2834.d: P2834 is the high-side counterpart: the fork A position input sits at the upper limit. In GM's 2023 Corvette table the rod 1 sensor is flagged when pulses stop and the pin voltage stays above 3.5 V, or when the duty cycle climbs over 92 %; after 150 ms a Type A fault is stored, but only while the sensor supply lies between 4.5 and 5.5 V and the battery between 8.75 and 18 V.
s: Warning lamp with stored code
Shifts on the affected shaft blocked
Reduced driveability in limp-home mode
c: Signal wire shorted to the 5 V sensor supply or battery voltage
Sensor output transistor no longer pulling low

P2835.d: P2835 covers a fork A position signal that is present but unsteady. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table checks the carrier frequency of the rod 1 sensor and sets a Type A fault once it leaves the 1500 to 2500 Hz band for 150 ms; Ford's 2024 summary calls the same check on the TR9070 frequency out of range.
s: Occasional refused or late shift
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Hesitation or no drive when pulling away
c: Intermittent contact at the sensor or module connector
Interference or damaged shielding on the signal line
Faulty Hall sensor in the shift drum motor (Ford DPS6)

P2836.d: P2836 is the umbrella circuit code for the shift fork B position input. Mercedes-Benz stores P283600 when its 8G-DCT dual-clutch transmission (724.1) detects an electrical defect at the fork B sensor and includes it in the code set evaluated by its Intelligent Predictive Repair routine in XENTRY.
s: Transmission warning and stored code
Gears of fork B skipped or unavailable
Delayed engagement from Park or no drive (Ford DPS6)
c: Electrical defect in the fork B position sensor (Mercedes 8G-DCT)
Failed current-control chip for the second shift drum motor in the TCM (Ford DPS6)
Corroded or loose contacts between sensor and module

P2837.d: P2837 flags a fork B position reading that is electrically sound but contradicts the gearbox state. GM's Corvette summary from 2023 maps fork B to rod 2 on the odd-gear shaft.
s: Gear jumps out or is not engaged on fork B
Noticeable pause or clunk while the gearbox retries the shift
Warning lamp and limited gear selection
c: Learned rod 2 positions no longer matching after repair or wear
Rod, fork or synchronizer binding so the gear does not engage or release cleanly
Sensor magnet or carrier loose on the rod
Blocked second shift drum motor (Ford DPS6)

P2838.d: P2838 is stored when the fork B position input reads at the bottom of its range. The Corvette's rod 2 sensor, fed by GM from the same 5 V reference A as rod 1, has to send a pulse-width signal; if pulses are missing while the pin is below 2.0 V, or the duty cycle drops under 8 %, the module waits 150 ms and logs a Type A fault.
s: Warning lamp with transmission in limp-home mode
Gears on rod 2 or fork B no longer selected
Rough or delayed shifts around the locked-out gears
c: Fork B sensor signal wire chafed through to ground
Sensor output no longer producing pulses
Break in the signal or supply wire leaving the input low

P2839.d: P2839 covers the other end of the scale: the fork B input is pinned high. GM's 2023 Corvette table for rod 2 sets it when pulses stop and the pin carries more than 3.5 V, or once the duty cycle passes 92 %.
s: Warning lamp and fault message in the cluster
Fork B gears blocked, fewer gears available
Reduced acceleration in the substitute program
c: Signal wire of the fork B sensor touching the 5 V or battery supply
Open sensor ground letting the output float high
Sensor output stage stuck in the high state

P283A.d: P283A means the fork B signal is arriving, but not cleanly. For rod 2 of the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox GM measures the period of the sensor carrier and reacts once the equivalent frequency drops below 1500 Hz or rises above 2500 Hz for 150 ms, logging a Type A fault.
s: Sporadic warning lamp that clears after a restart
Occasional hesitation or refused shift
Intermittent engagement problems when pulling away (Ford DPS6)
c: Loose or spread terminal in the fork B sensor connector
Electrical noise coupling into the signal line through damaged shielding
Faulty Hall element in the second shift drum motor (Ford DPS6)

P283B.d: P283B is the generic circuit code for the shift fork C position sensor. The only public manufacturer listing that uses it comes from Mercedes-Benz: on the 8G-DCT dual-clutch transmission (724.1) P283B00 stands for an electrical fault of the fork C sensor and belongs to the codes covered by its XENTRY repair routine for this gearbox.
s: Transmission warning in the instrument cluster
Gears handled by fork C no longer engaged
Emergency mode with reduced performance
c: Fork C position sensor with an internal electrical fault
Poor contact or moisture at the sensor or TCM connector
Damaged sensor input in the transmission control module

P283C.d: P283C is the plausibility code for fork C, which GM's 2023 Corvette table assigns to rod 3 on the even-gear shaft. Besides the force and speed comparison during shifts (over 600 N, more than 1100 µm off the learned point, Type A), a static monitor runs here: with no shift force on the rod, the reading must stay inside tolerance bands around the learned neutral or engaged point.
s: Even gears drop out or refuse to engage
Grinding or a knock during shifts on the even shaft
Warning lamp, gearbox limits gear choice
c: Rod 3 creeping out of position because of worn detent or fork
Position values not relearned after gearbox or sensor work
Synchronizer actuation on the even shaft not reaching target position

P283D.d: P283D reports the fork C input stuck low. In the Corvette dual-clutch gearbox GM feeds the rod 3 sensor from reference B rather than reference A, so its enable test watches that second 5 V rail and pauses while P0652 or P0653 are present.
s: Limp-home mode with warning lamp
Gears of fork C unavailable
Possibly further fork D codes if the shared supply is affected
c: Fork C signal line shorted to ground in the gearbox harness
Fork C sensor no longer switching its output
Damaged supply wire from reference B to the sensor

P283E.d: P283E is the high-side fault of the fork C circuit. GM's 2023 summary checks the Corvette rod 3 sensor for two signs: no pulses at all with the pin above 3.5 V, and a duty cycle above 92 %.
s: Warning lamp and gearbox fault message
Fork C gears locked out
Jerky driving in the substitute program
c: Pinched harness with the fork C signal touching a feed wire
Water in the connector bridging signal and supply pins
Fork C sensor without ground connection

P283F.d: P283F stands for an unstable fork C position signal rather than a hard short or open. The rod 3 sensor in GM's Corvette dual-clutch gearbox runs at a carrier between 1500 and 2500 Hz; if the measured period puts it outside that band for 150 ms, the module records a Type A fault, as long as reference B and battery voltage are valid.
s: Occasional stutter or delay on even-gear shifts
Warning lamp appears only now and then
c: Fork C connector working loose under engine movement
Cracked insulation near hot components letting noise in

P2840.d: P2840 is the overall circuit code for the shift fork D position input. Mercedes-Benz is the one maker that publicly documents it: in the 8G-DCT (transmission 724.1) of its compact models, P284000 marks an electrical fault of the fork D sensor, and the gearbox has a fifth fork E with its own codes from P2863 upward.
s: Gears of fork D withheld, gearbox skips them
Transmission warning lamp
Reduced driving comfort in emergency mode
c: Electrical failure of the fork D position sensor
Damaged wiring between fork D sensor and the TCM
Transmission control module input or software fault

P2841.d: P2841 indicates that fork D reports a believable voltage but an implausible position. GM's 2023 table runs the rod 4 consistency test in the Corvette only when neither the even-clutch speed signal nor the output speed signal has shown an electrical fault for at least 100 ms, so the comparison has trustworthy speeds behind it.
s: Hesitation or repeated attempts on even-gear shifts
Gear not held, slipping back to neutral
Warning lamp with reduced gear range
c: Rod 4 or its synchronizer sticking so the fork lags behind the command
Outdated learned positions after a clutch or sensor replacement
Fork D sensor or magnet shifted in its mount

P2842.d: P2842 sets when the fork D sensor signal collapses toward zero. GM's 2023 Corvette table expects a pulse train from the rod 4 sensor and flags the circuit if pulses vanish with less than 2.0 V present, or if the duty cycle is lower than 8 %, both held for 150 ms; the resulting fault is Type A.
s: Warning lamp, fork D gears blocked
Transmission in emergency program
Additional fork C code if the shared feed is at fault
c: Fork D signal wire shorted to ground or housing
No 5 V feed reaching the sensor

P2843.d: P2843 means the fork D position line is sitting near supply level. GM's 2023 Corvette table raises it for rod 4 when there is no pulse activity and more than 3.5 V on the pin, or when the duty cycle is above 92 %; after a 150 ms confirmation a Type A code is set.
s: Fault message and warning lamp
Some even gears no longer selected
Limp-home operation
c: Fork D signal wire in contact with a feed wire
Open ground circuit of the fork D sensor
Internal short in the sensor pulling its output high

P2844.d: P2844 points to a fork D signal whose timing wanders. GM's Corvette dual-clutch software derives the rod 4 sensor frequency from its period and expects 1500 to 2500 Hz; leaving that window for 150 ms stores a Type A fault, and the check is skipped while cranking or with reference B out of tolerance.
s: Sporadic hesitation on shifts
Warning lamp that may go out again
c: Chafed or loose harness section shared with the fork C sensor
Intermittent terminal contact at the fork D sensor
Sensor with an unstable output frequency

P2845.d: P2845 means the fork A sensor reports neutral although the gearbox state says a gear is engaged, or it reports an engaged position where neutral is expected. Public manufacturer documentation for P2845 is lacking, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 only asks that transmission inputs be checked for plausibility.
s: Gear display shows N while a gear is engaged, or the reverse
Shifts refused, transmission in limp-home mode
Warning lamp on
c: Neutral position not learned or lost after repair or software update
Sensor magnet or target shifted on the rod
Worn fork or detent changing the neutral position

P2846.d: P2846 flags a mismatch between the neutral reading of the fork B position sensor and the gear state the transmission module expects. Either the sensor claims fork B rests in neutral while the shaft speeds prove its gear carries load, or it reports an engaged fork where the module has commanded neutral.
s: Gears served by fork B refused or skipped
Transmission warning with reduced performance
Gear indicator disagrees with the actual gear
c: Learned neutral position of fork B missing after repair or module replacement
Magnet or target on the fork B rod loosened or shifted
Worn detent letting fork B settle off its neutral point

P2847.d: With P2847 the module has decided that the neutral signal from the fork C sensor cannot be trusted. Before a dual-clutch or automated manual box preselects a gear on a shaft, it must know that the other forks on that shaft are out; a false neutral could let two ratios mesh at once, so the module normally locks the affected gears out.
s: Gears of fork C locked out, jumps between remaining ratios
Warning lamp and stored transmission code
Harsh or delayed shifts on the affected shaft
c: Fork C sensor or magnet repositioned during transmission work without relearn
Fork C bent, so neutral lies outside the learned band
Position sensor output drifting with temperature or age

P2848.d: P2848 is the neutral-plausibility code for the fourth fork. It sets when the fork D sensor signal and the logical state of that fork disagree about neutral, even though the signal itself is electrically sound.
s: Gears of fork D unavailable
Drive system warning, emergency program
c: Fork D positions not relearned after software update or repair
Sensor of fork D loose in its mount
Wear on fork pads or synchronizer sleeve shifting the rest position

P2849.d: P2849 says that fork A did not travel when the module ordered it to, so its gear could not be put in or taken out. The reading may be valid; the fork itself is not following the command.
s: Gear of fork A will not engage or stays engaged
Limp-home mode with limited gears
Clunking or grinding during shift attempts
c: Shift rod of fork A seized in its bore or blocked by debris
Fork A actuator or its control valve not moving the rod
Broken fork or damaged synchronizer sleeve jamming the shift

P284A.d: P284A is stored when fork B stays put although the transmission module commanded a move, for instance from neutral toward an engaged gear or back. Published strategies avoid this code.
s: Gears of fork B missing or a gear stays engaged
Warning lamp and emergency mode
Rough starts or lack of drive in some gears
c: Fork B actuator, solenoid or hydraulic supply failing to apply force
Synchronizer of fork B gears jammed or damaged
Contaminated fluid restricting the fork B actuator

P284B.d: P284B reports a third fork that refuses to travel. Two situations matter: stuck in neutral, which merely costs the gears of fork C, and stuck in an engaged gear, which is more serious because that shaft then turns with a fixed ratio and a second gear on the same shaft must never be selected.
s: Car stays in one gear on one shaft or skips the fork C gears
Transmission warning lamp
c: Selector or pilot valve not routing pressure to the fork C rod
Fork C or its rod mechanically jammed

P284C.d: P284C applies when fork D, the fourth of the generic shift forks, fails to answer an actuation request. Whether the drive is hydraulic, as in most wet dual-clutch boxes, or electric, as in automated manuals with motor-driven drums, the module sees the request but no travel at the position sensor.
s: Gears of fork D unavailable or stuck engaged
Emergency program, reduced speed
Warning in the instrument cluster
c: Fork D actuator motor or hydraulic valve failed
Shift drum or rod binding at fork D
Module output stage not driving the fork D actuator

P284D.d: P284D means fork A has crept away from the position of the gear it is supposed to hold, without any shift being commanded. Several makers use it.
s: Message about a drive system fault with limited performance
First or seventh gear cannot be selected (Audi report)
Gear may jump out under load
c: Gear position sensors poorly calibrated (Audi DL382/DL552)
Leaking fork A actuator or weak detent letting the rod creep

P284E.d: P284E reports that fork B drifted while no shift was asked for. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table describes the test on rod 2 in detail: with no actuating force applied, the measured position must stay inside wide limits around the learned point of the gear verified as engaged by clutch-shaft and output speed readings; leaving them for 500 ms is a fault.
s: Gear on the odd shaft pops out or is re-engaged with a jolt
Warning lamp, possible limp-home mode
c: Synchronizer pressure valve for fork B leaking and pushing the rod
Weak detent or worn gear dog teeth on fork B gears

P284F.d: P284F covers drift of fork C away from its held gear. In GM's Corvette software this is rod 3, which sits on the shaft of the even clutch; the check compares the rod position with the learned point for the gear that the even clutch speed and the output speed confirm, and sets a Type A code once the wide limit is exceeded long enough or the drift correction keeps firing.
s: Even-shaft gear disengages unexpectedly
Shift flare or jerk while cruising
Warning lamp with stored code
c: Residual pressure on the fork C actuator from a leaking valve
Rod 3 sensor reading offset so the fork appears to move
Worn detent or synchronizer parts at fork C

P2850.d: P2850 closes the drift series for the four main forks: fork D has shifted position although the module neither commanded a change nor applied force to it. GM uses the code for rod 4 of the Corvette dual-clutch unit, again as a Type A fault that runs continuously and hands over to the even-shaft synchronizer recovery.
s: Gear of fork D slips out under load
Gears of fork D blocked, emergency program
c: Leaking synchronizer or selector valve moving the fork D rod
Positions not relearned after module or sensor replacement
Weak detent or rounded dog teeth on fork D gears

P2851.d: P2851 is meant for a plausibility comparison between the position sensors of forks A and B. Both readings may be in range on their own, yet together they describe an impossible state, such as both forks engaged at once, or they move in step in a way that points to a shared supply or ground fault.
s: Gears of forks A and B locked out
Warning lamp, limp-home mode
c: Shared supply or ground of the A and B sensors disturbed
One of the two sensors drifting while still in range
Corroded contacts at the internal transmission connector

P2852.d: P2852 pairs the position sensors of forks C and D and sets when their readings do not fit together. In GM's numbering these are rods 3 and 4, both on the even shaft and fed from the second sensor reference; a reference fault there would shift both signals together.
s: Gears of forks C and D unavailable
Transmission fault message, reduced power
c: Reference voltage feeding the C and D sensors out of tolerance
Sensor C or D reporting a shifted value
Input circuit fault in the transmission module

P2853.d: P2853 is set when the pressure measured at clutch A falls short of what the control model predicts. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table applies it to clutch 1, the odd-gear clutch, as a Type A fault in two ways: the model expects more than 1 bar while the sensor shows under 0.5 bar for 5 s, or the measured value stays below the model by more than a calibrated margin for too long.
s: Weak or delayed launch, engine flares
Odd gears unavailable, limp-home mode
Warning lamp on
c: Clutch A pressure control valve sticking or delivering too little
Leaking seal or piston ring in the clutch A circuit
Low fluid level or clogged filter reducing supply pressure

P2854.d: P2854 is the even-side partner of P2853: the pressure sensor of clutch B reports less than the control model expects. In GM's Corvette software clutch 2 drives the even gears; the check uses the same logic as on clutch 1, with a modeled value above 1 bar facing a reading under 0.5 bar for 5 s, plus a second path that watches the absolute gap between model and sensor.
s: Even gears skipped, car runs in odd gears only
Slipping or flare on shifts into even gears
Transmission warning
c: Clutch B pressure control valve restricted by debris or wear
Seal leak in the clutch B feed or piston
Foamed or overheated fluid lowering effective pressure

P2855.d: P2855 points the other way from P2853: clutch A carries more pressure than the model calls for. GM's Corvette table for clutch 1 uses three paths, all Type A.
s: Harsh engagement or jerky creep from standstill
Drag felt as if the brakes were applied
Limp-home mode with warning lamp
c: Clutch A pressure control valve sticking toward high output
Excessive line pressure feeding the clutch circuit
Clutch adaptation values out of date after repair

P2856.d: P2856 flags too much pressure at clutch B, the even-gear clutch in GM's and Ford's dual-clutch layouts. For the Corvette unit GM checks clutch 2 with the same high-side logic as clutch 1, including the hold-pressure case: an open clutch held at its standby pressure must not rise well above that point, because it would then pass torque while the other clutch is driving.
s: Shudder or binding during shifts
Even gears blocked, emergency program
Warning lamp
c: Clutch B pressure control valve hanging in a high-pressure position
Safety shutdown valve for clutch B not venting
Clutch B pressure sensor reading high within its range

P2857.d: P2857 reports that clutch A did not build up enough holding force when the control unit asked it to engage, so the expected ratio or torque transfer never appeared. Mitsubishi documents it for the CVT with two-speed auxiliary gearbox fitted to Mirage and Mirage G4 models from 2014 to 2022: while that gearbox is shifted into its first ratio, a measured ratio of 2.232 or more for 2 s counts as a fault, provided the ped
s: Engine speed flares on take-off without matching acceleration
Hesitation or reduced power, transmission emergency mode
Warning lamp with stored transmission code
c: Control valve (valve body) not delivering the commanded apply pressure to clutch A
Worn clutch A linings or leaking piston seals
Low, aerated or aged transmission fluid

P2858.d: P2858 is the clutch B counterpart of P2857: the element that should close for the second stage never reaches the pressure needed to carry torque. In Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT the check runs while the auxiliary gearbox changes up to its second ratio; if the ratio still reads 2.232 or higher after at least 2 s, the TCM concludes the box is hanging in neutral between the stages.
s: Second stage or even gears engage late or not at all
Engine revs rise at cruising speed, acceleration lags
Reduced power with warning lamp
c: Control valve unable to raise clutch B pressure
Slip damage inside the transmission (belt, clutch B linings)
Fluid level or quality outside specification

P2859.d: P2859 concerns the release side of clutch A: during a ratio change the control unit sees that the pressure handover is not working as planned, so the old and new power paths overlap or the wrong ratio persists. Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT shows how this is tested.
s: Harsh, doubled or tied-up shifts
Wrong gear stage held, engine speed too low or too high
Transmission warning and emergency program
c: Outgoing clutch not venting in time, so both elements carry torque
Sticking pressure control solenoid or valve in the valve body
Clutch pressure switch reporting pressure that is not there

P285A.d: With P285A the module reports a release-side pressure fault involving clutch B. Mitsubishi's Mirage CVT evaluates it while the auxiliary gearbox is commanded into its second stage: a ratio that remains within 10 % of the first stage (1.639–2.003) for 0.5 s, or that drops to 0.500 or below or climbs to 1.500 or above for 0.2 s, sets the code.
s: Upper stage or even gears not available
Flare between shifts, then a hard engagement
Limp mode with warning lamp
c: Defective control valve, especially when P0875 is stored at the same time
Leak in the clutch B circuit preventing a clean handover
Faulty clutch pressure switch or its wiring

P285B.d: P285B covers the electrical drive of the actuator that moves fork A, for designs where an electric motor rather than oil pressure shifts the gears. The module sets it when the output stage sees no load, typically a broken winding, a cut lead or a connector that has backed out.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and transmission warning
First, third or fifth gear not available, car may only move in the even gears
Jerky starts or refusal to pull away
c: Loose, corroded or backed-out connector at the fork A actuator motor
Broken lead between transmission module and actuator motor
Open phase winding inside the actuator motor
Failed motor output stage in the transmission module

P285C.d: P285C is the functional counterpart to the electrical fork A actuator codes. The circuit may be intact, yet the actuator does not achieve what it is asked to do: it moves too slowly, draws an unexpected current or leaves the fork short of its target.
s: Slow or harsh shifts into the gears of fork A
Wrench or transmission warning without engine lamp
Occasional gear skipping or neutral moments
c: Worn or sluggish fork A actuator motor
Shift drum, rod or fork A binding mechanically
Worn reduction gearing between motor and drum
Low supply voltage to the module during shifts

P285D.d: P285D points to a fork A actuator line pulled toward ground: a chafed motor phase touching the case, water in the connector, or a short inside the motor. To protect its driver, the module normally shuts the output down at once.
s: Engine lamp on, odd gears locked out
Car starts in second gear or will not move off
Code returns immediately after clearing
c: Actuator motor lead chafed through against the transmission case
Water or corrosion in the actuator connector
Internal short of a motor winding to its housing

P285E.d: P285E is logged when a line of the fork A actuator carries supply voltage where the module expects it to be switched low. Usual explanations are a harness short to a battery-fed wire or a low-side transistor in the module that no longer turns on; with some driver designs, an unloaded output can also read high.
s: Engine lamp lit, gears 1, 3 and 5 unavailable
Gearbox stays in an even gear or neutral
c: Actuator lead shorted to a battery-fed wire in the harness
Low-side driver in the transmission module not switching
Bridged pins in the actuator or module connector

P285F.d: With P285F the module reports that the drive circuit of the fork B actuator is open: current cannot flow when the motor or valve is energised. In Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch box, the second shift drum is turned by its own three-phase motor and places the forks for reverse plus 2nd, 4th and 6th; an open motor circuit there is P285F and requests the MIL.
s: No reverse gear, even gears missing
Engine lamp and gearbox fault message
Car drives only in 1st, 3rd and 5th with large rpm steps
c: Fork B actuator connector loose or with spread terminals
Open wire in the harness to the fork B actuator
Burnt or broken winding in the fork B motor

P2860.d: P2860 says the fork B actuator is electrically present but underperforms: travel takes too long, the target position is missed, or the effort needed to move it is out of line with what the module expects. No maker has published how it detects P2860.
s: Delayed engagement of reverse or the even gears
Wrench lamp or gearbox message, engine lamp off
Clunk or shudder during upshifts to 2nd, 4th or 6th
c: Stiff shift drum, rod or fork B
Fork B actuator motor with worn bearings or brushes
Debris or wear in the selector track

P2861.d: P2861 is set when a fork B actuator line reads near ground although the module has not switched it there, the classic signature of a short to ground. Ford's 2012 DPS6 summary assigns exactly this case on the motor of the drum for reverse and the even gears to P2861, and the 2014 Ford catalogue marks it as a MIL fault.
s: Reverse not selectable
Engine lamp on, only odd gears in use
c: Fork B motor lead rubbed through on a bracket or the case
Corrosion bridging a terminal to ground in the connector
Fork B motor winding shorted to its housing

P2862.d: P2862 indicates that a fork B actuator line sits at or near battery voltage when it should be pulled low. In practice this is a short to a powered conductor or a module transistor that stays open.
s: Engine lamp, no reverse or stuck in one even gear
Large rpm jumps because only odd gears are used
c: Fork B actuator wire shorted to a powered conductor
Module output transistor for fork B stuck
Insulation melted near the exhaust or a hot component

P2863.d: P2863 is the general circuit code for the position sensor of a fifth shift fork, used where the module cannot or does not distinguish between low, high and erratic signals. Only transmissions with five forks need it, such as eight-speed dual-clutch units.
s: Gears on fork E blocked, drive continues in remaining gears
Drive system warning in the instrument cluster
Unusual shift sequence or skipped gears
c: Poor contact at the fork E sensor or module connector
Fork E position sensor failed internally
Sensor reference supply shared with other sensors disturbed

P2864.d: P2864 sets when the fork E position signal is electrically fine but contradicts what the shaft speeds show. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table uses it as the Type A consistency check of rod 5, which belongs to the even-gear clutch shaft.
s: Gears on fork E locked out, warning lamp on
Harsh or aborted shifts on the even shaft
Reduced performance mode
c: Learned positions of rod 5 missing or outdated after repair or software update
Sensor magnet on the fork E rod shifted or loose
Synchronizer actuation valve for rod 5 sticking, so the rod barely moves
Implausible even-shaft or output speed signal misleading the check

P2865.d: P2865 means the fork E position input is stuck low. On GM's 2023 Corvette, whose rod 5 sensor sends a pulse-width signal, the TCM runs two Type A checks under this number: no pulses at all while the pin rests below 2000 mV, or a duty cycle under 8 %, each confirmed after 150 ms.
s: Warning lamp with fork E gears blocked
Fault returns at once after clearing
c: Fork E sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Fork E sensor with internal short or failed output stage
Sensor supply missing because of an open feed

P2866.d: P2866 is the high-level fault of the fork E sensor input. GM's Corvette TCM, reading rod 5 as a pulse-width signal, stores it as Type A in two situations: the line delivers no pulses and stays above 3500 mV, or the duty cycle climbs past 92 %.
s: Gears of fork E withheld, warning shown
Engine lamp after a short drive
c: Fork E signal wire touching a supply voltage wire
Open ground of the fork E sensor letting the signal float high
Sensor electronics holding the output permanently high

P2867.d: P2867 reports that the fork E sensor signal is present but unsteady. GM's Corvette TCM times each cycle of the digital rod 5 signal and sets the code, Type A, when the frequency drops below 1500 Hz or rises above 2500 Hz for at least 150 ms, with the same voltage and cranking exclusions as the low and high tests.
s: Sporadic warning, sometimes without noticeable effect
Occasional lockout of fork E gears
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the fork E sensor circuit
Damaged shielding letting electrical noise into the signal
Sensor electronics failing intermittently when hot

P2868.d: P2868 concerns the neutral information from the fork E sensor. The signal is electrically valid, but the module judges that the neutral it shows does not fit the real state of the fifth fork, either neutral claimed while a gear on that fork transmits drive, or a fork that seems engaged where neutral has been commanded.
s: Gears served by fork E refused
Gear display does not match the gear actually engaged
Warning lamp with limp-home program
c: Learned neutral of fork E lost after module swap or repair
Magnet or target on the fork E rod displaced
Worn detent or bent fork moving the rest position

P2869.d: P2869 states that fork E does not follow its commands: a gear on that fork cannot be engaged or released, although the position input itself may be working. No manufacturer publishes a strategy for P2869; the basis is the CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 requirement to check transmission components for function.
s: One gear stays engaged or cannot be selected
Transmission emergency mode, warning lamp
Grinding or clunking from the gearbox
c: Fork E rod seized in its bore or blocked by debris
Actuator or hydraulic valve of fork E not moving the rod
Synchronizer or sleeve of fork E jammed or broken

P286A.d: P286A flags fork E creeping out of the position that belongs to its current gear, although no shift was requested and no force is being applied. GM uses the code in the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM as the Type A drift fault of rod 5: as long as even clutch speed and output speed confirm the gear the module believes is engaged, the measured rod position must stay inside wide tolerance limits around that gear, and lea
s: Gear on fork E jumps out or shudders under load
Unexpected reshift or brief loss of drive
Warning lamp and stored transmission code
c: Weak detent spring or worn detent notch on the fork E rod
Leaking synchronizer actuation valve pushing the rod
Position reference of rod 5 lost after repair

P286B.d: P286B means the pressure applied to clutch A during engagement exceeded the level the control unit had planned. A clutch pressed too hard closes abruptly, which shows up as a jolt, a harsh launch or a shunt through the driveline.
s: Harsh launch or jolt when clutch A closes
Clunk through the driveline during shifts
Warning lamp, possibly limp mode
c: Clutch A pressure control valve sticking towards high output
Clutch adaptation values missing or wrong after repair or software update
Clutch pressure sensor reading higher than actual

P286C.d: P286C sets when clutch A still holds too much pressure while it is supposed to open. The residual force keeps the clutch dragging, so in a dual-clutch or planetary layout two power paths can briefly work against each other; the result is shudder, a braking feel during shifts or creeping with neutral selected.
s: Shudder or binding during shifts
Vehicle creeps or feels braked in neutral
Clutch overheating warning possible
c: Valve or exhaust passage for clutch A not venting fully
Debris or clutch material in the valve body
Pressure sensor showing residual pressure that is not real

P286D.d: P286D sets when clutch A takes longer to engage than the control unit allows. Volvo uses it in the inverter module (IEM) of the electric rear axle drive on its T8 plug-in hybrids: the rear e-motor is coupled to the wheels through a clutch, and when coupling is too slow, electric rear drive and all-wheel drive drop out and the MIL may light.
s: Electric rear drive or all-wheel drive unavailable
Delayed engagement with a pause in drive
MIL or hybrid warning
c: Outdated control module calibration (Volvo IEM software)
Slow clutch fill from low, aerated fluid or a restricted feed
Internal fault of the clutch or drive unit

P286E.d: P286E is the opposite of P286D: clutch A reaches its engaged state sooner than the control unit expects. An overly quick engagement usually means the fill phase is being skipped, because the piston was already partly applied, the pressure control overshoots or adaptation values are too aggressive; the driver feels a bang on take-off or during shifts.
s: Bang or jerk when clutch A engages
Harsh take-off from standstill
c: Clutch adaptation values too aggressive or not matched to new parts
Pressure control overshooting due to a sticking solenoid
Clutch piston not fully retracted before the next apply

P286F.d: P286F tells that clutch A needs too long to release. Torque then keeps flowing after the control unit has ordered the clutch open, which disturbs shifts and can make the vehicle creep or stall the engine at a stop.
s: Shudder or clunk on shifts out of odd gears
Creeping or engine stalling when stopping
MIL on, reduced function
c: Control module software needing an update (Ford PCM/TCM, Volvo IEM)
Release mechanism or return spring of clutch A sticking
Clutch wear shifting the release point beyond the learned value

P2870.d: P2870 flags clutch A opening faster than the control unit intended. During a shift the outgoing clutch has to pass torque smoothly to the incoming one; if it lets go too early, engine speed flares and the shift feels like a slip followed by a thump.
s: Engine flare during shifts, then a thump
Firmer substitute shift program
c: Leaking clutch A piston seal letting pressure drop too fast
Pressure control valve venting faster than commanded
Adaptation values not suited to the current clutch condition

P2871.d: P2871 means clutch A does not close, or slips so much that it behaves as if open. Mitsubishi documents this for the clutch in the front transaxle of the 2023 Outlander PHEV, which links the engine to the wheels in parallel mode: once parallel mode has been active for 2 s, the PHEV-ECU counts how often the speeds before and after the clutch differ by 75 rpm or more for 2 s, and after eight such events the code sets an
s: Engine cannot drive the wheels directly, only series or electric drive
Engine speed rises without extra thrust
MIL on
c: Worn clutch A that slips under load
Low transaxle fluid or external leak
Valve body, oil pump, pressure regulator or relief valve not supplying pressure
Control unit fault or outdated software

P2872.d: P2872 is set when clutch A stays closed although it should be open. Mitsubishi's 2023 Outlander PHEV uses it for the engine clutch in the front transaxle: in EV mode, or in series mode where an open clutch would leave a large speed gap, the front motor turns at 750 rpm or more, yet input and output of the clutch differ by 8 rpm or less for 3.5 s.
s: Engine turns with the wheels in EV mode, unusual noise or drag
Engine stalls when the vehicle stops
Hybrid system warning and MIL
c: Clutch A plates seized or welded together
Foreign material holding the proportional valve in the apply position
Control unit commanding or reading clutch state incorrectly

P2873.d: P2873 is set when clutch B is applied with more pressure than planned while it engages. In dual-clutch designs clutch B usually carries the even gears and reverse, as in Ford's DPS6 and GM's Corvette unit, so the fault tends to surface as jerky shifts into second, fourth or reverse and a hard bite when manoeuvring.
s: Jerky shifts into even gears or reverse
Hard bite when manoeuvring
Warning lamp, limp mode possible
c: Clutch B pressure control solenoid sticking high
Drifted or reset adaptation values for clutch B

P2874.d: P2874 indicates that clutch B keeps excess pressure while it is being released or should already be open. Clutch B then goes on carrying torque alongside the engaged path, which can be felt as binding, vibration during upshifts from even gears or a car that pulls while in neutral; an overheated clutch is a typical consequence.
s: Binding or vibration on upshifts from even gears
Car pulls in neutral
Clutch temperature warning
c: Clutch B valve not venting pressure on release
Contamination in the valve body from clutch wear
Seized shutdown valve or clutch B actuator

P2875.d: P2875 tells that clutch B takes too long to grip once the control unit has asked for it. Slow filling leaves a gap in drive during shifts into the gears served by clutch B, with a flare of engine speed before the clutch finally holds.
s: Delayed shifts into even gears with engine flare
Noticeable pause in drive during shifts
Warning lamp
c: Low or aerated fluid slowing the fill of clutch B
Partly blocked filter or valve passage
Worn seals leaking while the clutch fills

P2876.d: P2876 flags clutch B closing faster than its programmed fill and apply profile allows. Instead of a smooth handover the clutch grabs abruptly, which is often noticed as a knock when selecting reverse or when a dual-clutch box shifts into an even gear.
s: Knock when engaging reverse or even gears
Abrupt, harsh shifts
c: Adaptation values not relearned after clutch or mechatronic work
Clutch B solenoid overshooting its target pressure
Software calibration fault in the control unit

P2877.d: P2877 means clutch B releases too slowly after the command to open. While it lingers, the outgoing clutch fights the incoming one, so shifts out of even gears and reverse feel heavy, the car may shudder or the engine can be pulled down at a stop.
s: Heavy or shuddering shifts out of even gears and reverse
Engine pulled down or stalling at a stop
MIL on
c: Clutch B actuator or return spring not opening the clutch quickly
Clutch B wear or glazing changing the release behaviour
Restricted vent path on wet-clutch systems

P2878.d: P2878 reports that clutch B lets go sooner or more abruptly than the release ramp held in the control unit. During a powershift the outgoing clutch has to keep carrying torque until the incoming one has taken over; if clutch B drops out early, the engine flares for a moment and the next gear arrives with a jolt, mostly on shifts away from reverse and the even gears.
s: Brief engine flare followed by a jolt when shifting
Harsh shifts out of even gears or reverse
Warning lamp, firmer substitute shift program
c: Clutch B adaptation values no longer matching the linings
Actuator position count lost or misread by the hall sensors
On wet systems a clutch B valve venting pressure too quickly
Low fluid level or aerated fluid

P2879.d: P2879 is set when clutch B does not reach the torque it is asked for, or stays open altogether, so a large speed difference remains across it. No manufacturer publishes a test written for P2879.
s: Reverse or even gears missing
Engine speed rises without thrust
MIL and limp mode
c: Worn or glazed clutch B slipping under load
Insufficient apply pressure from valve body, pump or regulator
Clutch B actuator motor or its drive failed
Wiring fault or control unit not commanding the clutch

P287A.d: P287A means clutch B stays closed, or keeps transmitting torque, at a moment when it should be open. Ford lists P287A as an MIL code in its 2014 code catalogue.
s: Shudder or binding, strong pull in neutral
Engine stalls when the car stops
MIL on, gears locked out
c: Clutch B actuator or return spring not opening the clutch
Clutch B plates seized or welded after overheating
On wet systems a valve held in the apply position by debris
Control unit or wiring commanding apply continuously

P287B.d: P287B says that the control unit has no valid learned reference positions for shift fork A and therefore cannot place it accurately in neutral or in its gears. On electrically shifted dual-clutch boxes such as Ford's DPS6, drum A moves the forks for 1st, 3rd and 5th; the TCM knows each detent only as an angle, roughly 10, 90 and 190 degrees, derived from hall sensors on a motor that turns 61.44 times per drum revolut
s: Odd gears engage late, roughly or not at all
MIL or transmission warning
Learn procedure with scan tool does not complete
c: TCM replaced or reprogrammed without running the fork learn
Learn routine aborted by low voltage or other fault codes
Fork A position or drum fault preventing a valid learn
Worn fork, drum groove or detent

P287C.d: P287C means the transmission controller finds its trim or adaptation data missing, invalid or unfinished. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch TCM runs the check at initialisation, covering end-of-line and online values such as clutch preload, kiss point, fill volume, rod and parking lock positions, and learn routines left incomplete; the code is Type C, without MIL.
s: Rough or inconsistent shifts after TCM work
Learn or teach-in procedure refused
Transmission warning, often without MIL
c: Replacement TCM installed without trim or learn data
Initial start-up or learn routine not completed
Stored data rejected after a software update
Memory fault inside the control unit

P287D.d: P287D means the motor of the electric auxiliary transmission pump produces a torque outside its expected band, as estimated by the pump controller from phase current and speed. Too little torque hints at a pump that runs dry or draws air; too much hints at a dragging rotor, cold thick fluid or a blocked passage.
s: Start-stop or electric drive no longer available
Harsh engagement after engine restart
MIL on
c: Low fluid or air drawn into the auxiliary pump
Dragging pump rotor or blocked suction or delivery path
Worn pump motor or faulty integrated controller

P287E.d: In a parallel hybrid, the engine disconnect clutch (often called K0) sits between the combustion engine and the electric motor and is opened for electric driving. P287E reports that the control module sees no plausible current path through the actuator that operates this clutch, typically a pressure control solenoid in the transmission valve body or an electric actuator.
s: Malfunction or transmission warning in the instrument cluster
Engine does not start or cannot drive the wheels
Reduced power or limp-home operation
c: Loose, corroded or water-damaged connector at the transmission or actuator
Broken wire in the actuator feed or return line
Open coil in the clutch pressure solenoid or actuator
Failed output stage in the transmission or hybrid control module

P287F.d: P287F concerns the actuator of the clutch that couples the engine to the electric motor of a parallel hybrid. The circuit is not broken; instead, the electrical feedback (current, voltage or duty cycle) does not match what the control module expects for its command, or the clutch reacts to the command differently than the model predicts.
s: Jerky or delayed engine engagement when switching from electric to hybrid mode
Transmission warning, sometimes only intermittently
Limited hybrid functions or limp-home operation
c: Clutch solenoid or actuator with drifting resistance or sticking spool
Low, aged or contaminated transmission fluid
Lost clutch adaptation values or outdated control software
High contact resistance at connector pins

P2880.d: P2880 is stored when the signal in the actuator circuit of the engine disconnect clutch stays below its permitted window. In practice this usually means a short to ground on the control side, or a feed that has lost supply voltage, so that the solenoid or actuator is either energised permanently or not at all, depending on which side is affected.
s: Hybrid or transmission warning lamp
Engine cannot be coupled, only electric driving available
Limp-home mode after the output is switched off
c: Chafed control wire shorted to ground or housing
Missing supply voltage (fuse, relay, feed wire)
Internal short in the clutch solenoid coil
Faulty output stage in the control module

P2881.d: P2881 is the counterpart to P2880: the monitored signal in the circuit of the disconnect clutch actuator is above the upper limit. A control line touching battery voltage is the textbook case; an open return line or a missing ground at a low-side driver can produce the same reading, because the module then sees full voltage where it expects a pulled-down level.
s: Warning lamp with hybrid system message
Harsh or missing engine engagement
Limited driving mode
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Open return line or missing ground on the actuator
Moisture bridging pins in the transmission connector
Faulty voltage sensing in the control module

P2882.d: P2882 means the clutch between combustion engine and electric motor slips more than allowed while it is supposed to be closed: the speed on the engine side and the speed on the motor side drift apart. Audi documents this code (P288200, symptom 20954) for the Q5 e quattro of 2020–2024 and the A7 e quattro of 2021–2022; the driver sees a gearbox fault message, and the code is stored in the engine control module.
s: Gearbox malfunction message in the cluster
Engine revs flare while torque on the wheels lags behind
Hybrid mode limited, more electric-only operation
c: Transmission or electric drive software with faulty slip evaluation
Low transmission fluid level reducing clutch pressure
Clutch touch point not or wrongly adapted
Worn clutch plates or leaking hydraulic seal

P2883.d: P2883 protects the disconnect clutch from overheating. Most systems do not measure the friction plates directly; the control module models their temperature from slip speed, transmitted torque and fluid temperature, and sets the code when the estimate passes its limit.
s: Warning to let the transmission cool down
Reduced power or restricted starting off
Smell of hot fluid after heavy use
c: Heavy load such as towing, creeping or stop-and-go on grades
Clutch slipping due to low pressure or wear
Restricted transmission fluid cooling or low fluid level
Temperature model in the control software too conservative

P2884.d: P2884 reports that the disconnect clutch stays open although the control module has asked it to close, so the running engine cannot pass torque to the transmission. Audi documented the code (P288400, held in the gearbox module J217) on the 2016–2017 A3 e-tron: a gearbox warning and limp-home mode, traced to a mechanically defective pressure valve of clutch 0; if it is the only stored code, the mechatronic unit is rep
s: Gearbox warning or wrench indicator
Engine runs but does not drive the vehicle
Limp-home or electric-only driving
c: Faulty clutch pressure regulating valve in the mechatronic unit
Insufficient hydraulic pressure (fluid level, pump, leak)
Mechanical damage in the clutch pack or piston

P2885.d: P2885 is the more general engagement code: the clutch does close, but the process does not run as planned – it takes too long, synchronisation of engine and motor speed fails, or torque arrives with a jolt. It does not claim that the clutch is permanently open or closed; those cases have P2884 and P2886.
s: Jolt or hesitation when the engine is coupled in
MIL or wrench indicator
Hybrid mode restricted
c: Outdated software in hybrid, transmission or engine control module
Weak hydraulic supply, e.g. auxiliary pump or low fluid
Clutch fill and touch point adaptation out of range
Faulty speed signal on engine or motor side

P2886.d: P2886 is the opposite failure to P2884: the control module commands the disconnect clutch to open, yet engine and electric motor keep turning together. The engine is then dragged along during electric driving, which costs range and can stall it when the vehicle stops.
s: Engine turns during electric driving or stalls when stopping
Reduced electric range
Warning lamp and restricted hybrid mode
c: Clutch control valve stuck in the apply position
Residual pressure from a blocked drain or faulty pump control
Control software misjudging the clutch state

P2887.d: P2887 is the general circuit code for the actuator that engages and releases the park lock in park-by-wire transmissions. It covers faults that are not specifically open, low or high, and some manufacturers use it as a base code that carries a failure-type byte.
s: Transmission service message or warning lamp
P cannot be selected or released reliably
c: Control software misjudging the actuator circuit
Loose, corroded or damaged actuator connector or harness
Park lock actuator or hold solenoid sticking or failed

P2888.d: P2888 flags an open circuit in the park lock actuator path: the output stage switches on but finds no load. Ford's 2024-25 OBD summary maps it, alongside P2887_13, for the 8F24, 8F35/8F40 and 8F57 front-drive automatics, and in the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox as an open load on the parking lock hold solenoid, where it can also be reported as P2887_01.
s: Vehicle stays in P or will not accept a gear
Shift system warning
c: Broken wire or backed-out terminal at the actuator connector
Open coil in the park lock actuator or hold solenoid
Output stage in the control unit not switching

P2889.d: P2889 reports that the park lock actuator circuit sits lower than it should, as a rule because the line touches ground. Ford's 2024-25 summary pairs it with P2887_11, a short to ground, on the 8F24, 8F35/8F40 and 8F57 automatics; for the TR9070 dual-clutch unit it is called a shorted switch on the parking lock hold solenoid, meaning the switching side of the stage is pulled to ground.
s: Park lock function blocked, warning shown
Difficulty selecting or leaving P
c: Harness chafed through and shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the actuator connector
Actuator coil shorted to its housing

P288A.d: P288A is set when the park lock actuator circuit reads higher than allowed, typically because it has contact with battery voltage or the load itself is shorted. Ford's 2024-25 summary books it as P2887_12, short to power, on Ford's three transverse 8-speed automatics (8F24, 8F35/8F40, 8F57); on the TR9070 dual-clutch transmission the same code stands for a shorted load on the parking lock hold solenoid, so the coil r
s: Shift system warning, park lock function switched off
Car stays in its last position, P or drive range
c: Control line shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Shorted turns in the actuator or hold solenoid coil

P288B.d: P288B means the park lock actuator is electrically intact but does not do what it is told, for example the lock fails to move in time. Ford's 2024-25 summary calls it functionally stuck off on its front-drive 8-speeds and mechanically stuck off on the TR9070 dual-clutch box.
s: P cannot be selected or needs several attempts to leave
Unexpected shift to P during start-stop
Warning lamp or MIL
c: Control software needing an update (Ford, Nissan, Audi, FCA)
Sluggish or sticking park lock actuator or pawl mechanism
Low supply voltage or poor connection under load

P288C.d: P288C does not look at the clutch itself but at the electronic switch inside the control module that powers its actuator. Modern driver chips measure their own current and junction temperature; if either exceeds the limit, they shut down and report this condition.
s: Clutch actuator switched off, engine cannot be coupled
Warning lamp, often after long or hot drives
Limp-home operation
c: Actuator coil or motor drawing excessive current
Partial short in the actuator wiring
Control module overheating from heat or poor cooling
Defective driver chip in the control module

P288D.d: P288D is the fork B counterpart of P287B: the stored learn values that tell the control unit where fork B or its drum sits in each gear are missing or rejected. No manufacturer documents P288D publicly, and Ford's 2014 catalogue still knew only one fork calibration code, P287B, which suggests the split into A and B came later.
s: Reverse or even gears hesitant or unavailable
Transmission warning, possibly MIL
c: Fork learn not carried out after TCM or mechatronic work
Drum B position or motor fault aborting the learn
Worn or bent fork B, worn drum groove

P288E.d: P288E is a self-protection code of the output stage that powers the actuator of shift fork A. The driver reports a current above its limit or an excessive chip temperature, and the module throttles or switches off that actuator.
s: Odd gears do not engage, car may start in 2nd
Transmission warning and limp mode
c: Shorted winding or lead in the fork A actuator circuit
Binding drum or fork stalling the actuator under full current
High transmission temperature adding heat to the driver
Defective driver stage in the control unit

P288F.d: P288F tells that the driver for the shift fork B actuator has crossed its current or temperature limit, after which the TCM curbs or stops the actuator to save the electronics. Public manufacturer criteria for P288F are not available.
s: Reverse not available, even gears skipped
Warning lamp and limp mode
