c: Short in the fork B actuator motor or its lead
Seized drum B or fork worn into its groove
Driver stage in the TCM failing

P2890.d: Some engines use the spark plug as a combustion sensor: between sparks a measuring voltage is applied, and the hot, ionised gas lets a small current flow whose shape reveals misfire and knock. P2890 is the basic circuit fault for this measurement on cylinder 1 – the module receives no usable ion signal from that cylinder at all.
s: MIL with reduced knock and misfire monitoring on cylinder 1
Longer cranking if cylinder identification is affected
Retarded ignition and less power as a precaution
c: Ignition coil of cylinder 1 with failed ion measuring stage
Open ion signal wire or connector between coil 1 and the processing module
Faulty ion processing module or engine control module input

P2891.d: Here the ion signal of cylinder 1 is present but implausible: its level or waveform does not fit engine speed and load, or it differs clearly from the other cylinders. Fouled or worn spark plugs are a frequent reason, since soot or oil deposits form a leakage path that distorts the small measuring current; a cracked insulator or water in the plug well has a similar effect.
s: MIL, sometimes together with misfire codes
Rough idle or hesitation
Reduced power due to cautious knock control
c: Sooted, oil-fouled or worn spark plug in cylinder 1
Moisture or oil in the plug well of cylinder 1
Ion measuring stage of coil 1 drifting
Real combustion fault in cylinder 1 (mixture, compression)

P2892.d: P2892 says the ion measurement of cylinder 1 delivers a signal that stays below the expected range. Electrically this points to a signal line shorted to ground or a measuring stage that no longer builds up its bias voltage; Saab, for example, applies around 120 V across the plug gap between sparks to obtain the current.
s: MIL and stored fault for cylinder 1
Noticeably less power from retarded ignition
Possibly unreported misfires on cylinder 1
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 1 shorted to ground
Coil 1 no longer generates its measuring voltage
Spark plug of cylinder 1 with leakage path through deposits

P2893.d: With P2893 the ion signal from cylinder 1 sits above its plausible ceiling. A signal line touching a supply voltage is the most direct explanation; crosstalk from the ignition primary circuit or a defective evaluation stage that saturates can show the same picture.
s: MIL with cylinder 1 ion fault
Reduced power and possibly higher fuel consumption
Knock may go unnoticed on cylinder 1
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 1 shorted to a voltage source
Internal fault in coil 1 coupling ignition voltage into the signal
Saturated input in the ion processing module

P2894.d: P2894 covers a general fault in the ion current circuit of cylinder 2: the processing electronics get no evaluable signal from this plug. Which physical position cylinder 2 occupies depends on the maker's numbering.
s: MIL with a stored cylinder 2 ion fault
Hard or longer starting in some cases
Cautious ignition timing and slightly less power
c: Ignition coil of cylinder 2 with dead ion measurement
Interrupted ion signal path from coil 2
Defective cylinder 2 input in the processing module

P2895.d: P2895 is set when cylinder 2 delivers an ion signal that is electrically intact but does not behave plausibly – for example, it shows almost no combustion peak at normal load, or it scatters strongly from cycle to cycle compared with the neighbouring cylinders. Because the ion current is a direct image of combustion, a genuine problem in cylinder 2 such as a lean injector, a leaking valve or low compression can trigg
s: MIL, sometimes with misfire code P0302
Uneven running felt mainly at idle
Increased fuel consumption
c: Worn or fouled spark plug in cylinder 2
Combustion fault in cylinder 2 (injector, valve, compression)
Coil 2 measuring stage drifting with temperature

P2896.d: P2896 reports a cylinder 2 ion signal that remains under its lower limit. A ground short on the line from coil 2, a cracked plug insulator that drains the measuring voltage to the cylinder head, or a coil whose bias generator has failed can all produce a near-zero reading.
s: MIL with ion fault on cylinder 2
Engine runs on a safe ignition map with less power
Misfire on cylinder 2 may not be detected
c: Chafed ion signal wire of cylinder 2 touching ground
Cracked spark plug insulator in cylinder 2
Measuring voltage generator in coil 2 failed

P2897.d: P2897 applies when the ion current reading of cylinder 2 is stuck above the range the module accepts. Typical electrical reasons are a signal line that has contacted a supply or ignition feed, a damaged coil 2 that leaks primary voltage into its measuring output, or a missing ground at the coil that shifts the reference.
s: MIL and stored cylinder 2 ion fault
Less power due to retarded timing on cylinder 2
Knock protection for cylinder 2 limited
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 2 in contact with a voltage source
Coil 2 leaking primary voltage into the measuring output

P2898.d: P2898 marks a basic circuit failure in the ion current measurement of cylinder 3: the engine computer receives nothing it can evaluate from that spark plug. With ion sensing, the plug doubles as a probe, because a bias voltage across the gap drives a small current through the burning, conductive gas.
s: MIL with ion fault stored for cylinder 3
Starting may take longer while cylinder identification is uncertain
Engine runs with cautious ignition timing and somewhat less power
c: Ignition coil of cylinder 3 whose ion measuring stage has failed
Loose or corroded connector at coil 3 or broken ion signal wire
Faulty cylinder 3 input in the ion processing module or engine module

P2899.d: With P2899 an ion signal from cylinder 3 does arrive, yet it fails the plausibility check: its amplitude is too weak for the current load, it fluctuates without reason, or it no longer matches the pattern of the remaining cylinders. Because the measurement mirrors how hot and how highly compressed the burning charge is, an actual combustion weakness in cylinder 3 can be the cause just as much as a degraded plug with
s: MIL, possibly together with P0303
Slight roughness at idle or under light load
Knock control retards timing more than usual
c: Spark plug of cylinder 3 with deposits or excessive gap wear
Weak combustion in cylinder 3 (lean injector, low compression)
Damaged plug boot or moisture at the coil 3 connection

P289A.d: P289A applies when the ion reading of cylinder 3 stays below the lower plausibility limit. Usually the signal path is pulled to ground somewhere, or the coil no longer supplies the measuring voltage of roughly 80 V that Saab's T7 cassette keeps across each gap between sparks.
s: MIL with low ion signal on cylinder 3
Misfire codes or no misfire detection for cylinder 3
Less power because timing is pulled back as a precaution
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 3 chafed through to ground
Carbon tracking or cracked insulator on the cylinder 3 plug
Coil 3 no longer builds up its measuring voltage

P289B.d: P289B signals that the ion channel of cylinder 3 sits permanently above its upper limit. A conductor touching battery voltage, a coil that couples ignition energy into its measuring output, or a lost ground reference are the usual electrical reasons.
s: MIL with high ion signal fault on cylinder 3
Knock on cylinder 3 may go undetected, so timing is retarded
Reduced pulling power
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 3 shorted to battery or supply voltage
Coil 3 coupling ignition energy into its measuring output
Missing ground reference at coil 3 or the processing module

P289C.d: P289C stands for a general circuit fault in the ion measurement of cylinder 4, meaning no usable signal reaches the evaluation electronics from that plug. Cylinder 4 has a special role in Saab's Trionic four-cylinders: without a camshaft sensor, the engine fires cylinders 1 and 4 at the same time during start-up and decides from the ion response which of them is on the compression stroke.
s: MIL with ion fault stored for cylinder 4
Extended cranking because cylinder 1 and 4 cannot be told apart reliably
Conservative ignition timing with reduced power
c: Ion measuring stage in the coil of cylinder 4 failed
Open circuit between coil 4 and the processing module
Cylinder 4 input of the processing module defective

P289D.d: P289D is a rationality fault: cylinder 4 supplies an ion trace that is electrically present but not credible, for instance a combustion peak far smaller than the others at equal load, or erratic changes between cycles. Low-pass filtering of this trace gives the combustion information, band-pass filtering the knock content, so a distorted signal degrades both functions for cylinder 4.
s: MIL, sometimes accompanied by P0304
Noticeable vibration at idle
Fuel consumption rises slightly
c: Worn or fouled spark plug in cylinder 4
Oil in the plug well of cylinder 4 from a leaking cover gasket
Mixture or compression problem in cylinder 4

P289E.d: P289E means the ion signal of cylinder 4 remains below the range the module expects. A ground fault on the line from coil 4, a plug whose insulator conducts the bias voltage away, or a coil that has stopped generating that voltage are the main suspects.
s: MIL with low ion signal on cylinder 4
Possible start delay or misfire codes
Power reduced by safety timing on cylinder 4
c: Ion signal line of cylinder 4 shorted to ground
Spark plug insulator of cylinder 4 leaking the bias voltage
Bias voltage generation inside coil 4 failed

P289F.d: P289F is set when the ion measurement of cylinder 4 is held above its plausible maximum. Electrically, look for a signal conductor in contact with a supply feed, an internally leaking coil 4, or a poor ground that lifts the reference level.
s: MIL with high ion signal on cylinder 4
Reduced performance from retarded ignition
Knock protection on cylinder 4 weakened
c: Ion signal conductor of cylinder 4 touching a supply feed
Internal leakage in coil 4 raising the measuring output
Poor ground lifting the reference of the cylinder 4 channel

P28A0.d: P28A0 reports that the ion current circuit of cylinder 5 delivers no evaluable signal. A cylinder 5 exists only on engines with five or more cylinders, which narrows the field considerably.
s: MIL with ion fault stored for cylinder 5
Misfire monitoring of cylinder 5 restricted
Retarded timing and slightly reduced power
c: Coil of cylinder 5 with failed ion measuring circuit
Connector or wire fault between coil 5 and the evaluation electronics

P28A1.d: P28A1 flags a cylinder 5 ion signal that is electrically intact but implausible in size or shape compared with load, speed and the other cylinders. Ion current rises with chamber pressure and temperature, so a lean or poorly compressing cylinder 5 produces a weak trace exactly like a fouled plug does.
s: MIL, possibly with misfire code P0305
Uneven running under load
Higher fuel consumption
c: Fouled or eroded spark plug in cylinder 5
Lean mixture in cylinder 5 from a clogged injector or intake leak

P28A2.d: P28A2 is stored when the cylinder 5 ion reading stays under its lower threshold. The measurement relies on a constant bias across the plug gap between sparks – about 80 V on Saab's T7 discharge modules – and anything that drains it to ground pulls the reading down: a chafed signal conductor, a cracked plug insulator, or a coil whose bias supply has failed.
s: MIL with low ion signal on cylinder 5
Misfire codes for cylinder 5 may appear
Safety ignition map reduces power
c: Signal conductor of cylinder 5 chafed against ground
Cracked insulator on the cylinder 5 spark plug

P28A3.d: P28A3 indicates a cylinder 5 ion signal locked above its permitted ceiling. Contact between the signal path and a voltage source, a coil 5 that injects ignition energy into its output, or a disturbed ground reference can cause it.
s: MIL with high ion signal on cylinder 5
Ignition retarded on cylinder 5, less power
Knock events may not be recognised
c: Signal path of cylinder 5 in contact with a voltage source
Coil 5 feeding ignition energy into its measuring output
Disturbed ground reference of the evaluation circuit

P28A4.d: P28A4 is the general circuit code for the ion measurement of cylinder 6: the electronics get no usable signal from that plug. Only engines with six or more cylinders are affected, and among them ion sensing is rare.
s: MIL with ion fault stored for cylinder 6
Reduced misfire and knock monitoring on cylinder 6
Moderate power loss from cautious timing
c: Ion measuring part of the cylinder 6 coil defective
Open ion signal circuit of cylinder 6 in the harness or connector

P28A5.d: P28A5 points to a cylinder 6 ion signal that exists but makes no sense for the operating point: too little combustion response, a trace that jumps between cycles, or one that departs from the remaining cylinders. Since ionisation follows the actual burn, a misfiring or lean cylinder 6 can trigger it as readily as a worn plug or a wet plug well.
s: MIL, often together with P0306
Rough running at idle or light throttle
Hesitation under acceleration
c: Spark plug of cylinder 6 worn or sooted
Water or oil in the plug well of cylinder 6
Poor combustion in cylinder 6 (injector, valve, compression)

P28A6.d: P28A6 describes an ion reading from cylinder 6 that never leaves the bottom of its range. Between sparks the system keeps a small voltage across the plug, and the hot gas of a normal combustion lets a measurable current pass; if that voltage leaks to ground through a damaged conductor, a cracked ceramic or carbon deposits, or the coil stops supplying it, the reading collapses.
s: MIL with low ion signal on cylinder 6
Misfires on cylinder 6 possibly unrecorded
Engine noticeably weaker on safe timing
c: Damaged ion conductor of cylinder 6 leaking to ground
Cracked ceramic or heavy deposits on the cylinder 6 plug
Coil 6 no longer supplies the measuring voltage

P28A7.d: P28A7 is logged when the ion signal of cylinder 6 is held above the upper limit the module accepts. A conductor in contact with battery voltage, crosstalk from the primary side of coil 6, or an evaluation stage driven into saturation are the typical electrical explanations.
s: MIL with high ion signal on cylinder 6
Less power because of late ignition on cylinder 6
Knock on cylinder 6 may not be detected
c: Ion conductor of cylinder 6 touching battery voltage
Crosstalk from the primary side of coil 6

P28A8.d: P28A8 covers a basic circuit fault in the ion current measurement of cylinder 7, so the module obtains no evaluable signal from that plug. A cylinder 7 only exists on engines with eight or more cylinders, and Saab, the best-known user of ion sensing, applied it to four-cylinder and V6 engines; no maker publicly describes an eight-cylinder version.
s: MIL with ion fault stored for cylinder 7
Misfire and knock monitoring of cylinder 7 unavailable
Some power loss from protective timing
c: Coil of cylinder 7 with defective ion measuring function
Broken wire or loose connector in the cylinder 7 ion circuit
Cylinder 7 input of the evaluation electronics faulty

P28A9.d: P28A9 means cylinder 7 returns an ion signal that is electrically sound but not believable for the current speed and load, or that stands out against the other cylinders of an eight-or-more-cylinder engine. Because the current through the plug gap grows with combustion pressure and temperature, a lean or misfiring cylinder 7 produces this picture as readily as a fouled plug or moisture in the well.
s: MIL, possibly together with P0307
Uneven idle
Knock control retards timing more often
c: Fouled or worn spark plug in cylinder 7
Lean mixture or misfire in cylinder 7
Moisture in the plug well of cylinder 7

P28AA.d: P28AA reports that the ion current reading from cylinder 7 has dropped below the floor the engine computer accepts. Ion sensing places a measuring voltage on the spark plug between firings; Saab's Trionic T8 coils generate about 120 V for this themselves.
s: MIL lit with a low ion reading stored for cylinder 7
Misfire code P0307 may appear although the engine runs smoothly
Reduced power from protective ignition timing
c: Carbon track inside the cylinder 7 plug boot
Ion signal lead of cylinder 7 rubbed through to ground
Split ceramic insulator on the cylinder 7 plug
Measuring-voltage stage in coil 7 no longer working

P28AB.d: P28AB is set when the cylinder 7 ion signal sits above the highest value a healthy measuring circuit can deliver. Typical triggers are a signal lead touching a supply wire, moisture bridging the coil connector, or a coil whose ignition pulse bleeds into its measuring output.
s: MIL lit with a high ion reading stored for cylinder 7
Genuine misfire on cylinder 7 may go unreported
Timing pulled back on cylinder 7, slightly less power
c: Ion signal lead of cylinder 7 touching a supply wire
Moisture bridging contacts in the coil 7 connector
Coil 7 leaking its ignition pulse into the measuring output

P28AC.d: P28AC flags a general electrical fault in the ion current path of cylinder 8, typically an open connection, so no usable signal reaches the evaluation electronics. On a V8 this is the highest-numbered cylinder, on V10 and V12 engines a middle one; which bank it sits on depends on the maker's numbering.
s: MIL with a circuit fault stored for cylinder 8
No misfire or knock assessment for cylinder 8
Engine may run with conservative timing and lower power
c: Loose or corroded connector in the cylinder 8 ion line
Broken conductor between coil 8 and the evaluation module
Cylinder 8 input of the evaluation module defective

P28AD.d: P28AD means the cylinder 8 ion signal is electrically intact but does not fit what the computer expects for the operating point, or it deviates clearly from the other cylinders. CARB treats such rationality checks as part of the monitoring of input components next to tests for wiring faults and for values outside the valid band.
s: MIL, often together with P0308
Rough running under load
Knock control intervenes more often on cylinder 8
c: Worn electrodes or wrong gap on the cylinder 8 plug
Oil deposits on the cylinder 8 plug

P28AE.d: P28AE stands for an ion reading from cylinder 8 that stays too low or near zero. Either the measuring voltage never reaches the plug, because the coil's bias stage or its supply has failed, or it drains away to ground through a damaged signal wire, a wet plug well or a tracked boot.
s: MIL lit with a low ion reading for cylinder 8
Knock protection of cylinder 8 lost, timing retarded
Possible misfire report for cylinder 8
c: Water or oil in the cylinder 8 plug well
Damaged cylinder 8 signal wire shorted to ground
Bias stage of coil 8 not producing measuring voltage

P28AF.d: P28AF is logged when cylinder 8 delivers an ion signal pinned at or above the upper limit. Possible reasons include the signal conductor shorted to battery voltage or to another live circuit in the harness, internal leakage inside coil 8 that lets the high-voltage side couple into the measuring line, or a lost reference ground at the evaluation input.
s: MIL lit with a high ion reading for cylinder 8
Misfire on cylinder 8 may stay undetected
Safety timing reduces power somewhat
c: Cylinder 8 signal conductor shorted to battery voltage
Internal leakage in coil 8 coupling into the measuring line
Lost reference ground at the evaluation input

P28B0.d: P28B0 marks an electrical circuit fault, usually an interruption, in the ion current measurement of cylinder 9. A ninth cylinder appears only on engines with ten or more cylinders, such as V10, V12 or W12 designs.
s: MIL with ion circuit fault for cylinder 9
Misfire and knock evaluation of cylinder 9 suspended
Slight loss of power from retarded timing
c: Coil 9 connector not latched or with spread terminals
Ion output of coil 9 without function
Interrupted ion line of cylinder 9 in the harness

P28B1.d: P28B1 indicates that cylinder 9 produces an ion signal of believable electrical level whose shape or strength does not match engine speed, load or the neighbouring cylinders. Since the reading reflects combustion pressure and temperature, the root cause is often mechanical or mixture-related: a worn or oil-fouled plug, a leaking valve, a weak injector on cylinder 9, or condensation in the plug well.
s: MIL, possibly with misfire code P0309
Noticeably uneven running at idle
Higher fuel consumption
c: Worn or oil-fouled spark plug in cylinder 9
Weak spray from the cylinder 9 injector
Condensation in the cylinder 9 plug well

P28B2.d: P28B2 is stored when the ion current measured at cylinder 9 remains under its lower plausibility limit. In an ion-sensing ignition each coil both fires the plug and supplies the measuring voltage, so a coil 9 with a weak bias stage, a cracked plug insulator or a signal wire grounded in the harness all reduce the current reaching the evaluator.
s: MIL with low ion reading on cylinder 9
P0309 often stored at the same time
Reduced power under load
c: Cylinder 9 signal wire grounded in the harness
Cracked insulator on the cylinder 9 plug

P28B3.d: P28B3 shows that the cylinder 9 ion signal is held above the range a working circuit produces. Shorts from the sense line to a powered conductor, a coil 9 leaking high-voltage energy into its measuring output, or water in the connector can push it there.
s: MIL with high ion reading on cylinder 9
Real misfire on cylinder 9 can go unnoticed
Timing on cylinder 9 retarded as a precaution
c: Cylinder 9 sense line shorted to a powered conductor
Coil 9 leaking high-voltage energy into its measuring output

P28B4.d: P28B4 is the basic circuit code for the ion current measurement of cylinder 10; typically the line from coil 10 to the evaluation module is interrupted or the coil's measuring stage is dead. Ten cylinders mean a V10 at minimum, where this is the last cylinder in the numbering, or a V12 or W12, where it is not.
s: MIL with ion circuit fault for cylinder 10
Cylinder 10 excluded from misfire and knock evaluation
Possible power reduction through protective timing
c: Open line between coil 10 and the evaluation module
Corroded terminals at the coil 10 connector

P28B5.d: P28B5 reports an ion signal from cylinder 10 that is electrically valid yet implausible: its amplitude or timing after the spark does not fit the load point or departs from the remaining cylinders. Because ionisation depends on how hot and dense the burning charge is, causes include an eroded electrode gap, oil-wetted plugs, mixture errors on cylinder 10 or a compression loss.
s: MIL, sometimes together with P0310
Erratic ignition timing on cylinder 10
Hesitation when accelerating
c: Eroded electrode gap on the cylinder 10 plug

P28B6.d: P28B6 is set when the cylinder 10 ion reading is persistently too low. The measuring bias that should sit across the gap between sparks is missing or being drained: a coil 10 whose bias generator has failed, conductive deposits bridging the plug insulator, a wet boot, or a sense wire with insulation damage touching ground.
s: MIL with low ion reading on cylinder 10
P0310 may be stored as well
Cautious ignition timing, less pulling power
c: Conductive deposits bridging the cylinder 10 plug insulator
Cylinder 10 sense wire with damaged insulation touching ground

P28B7.d: P28B7 means the ion signal of cylinder 10 is stuck above its valid window. The usual suspects are a sense lead shorted to a supply or to a neighbouring ignition circuit, breakdown inside coil 10 that lets spark energy into the measuring path, and a poor ground at the evaluation side that shifts the reference upward.
s: MIL with high ion reading on cylinder 10
Timing on cylinder 10 retarded for safety
Misfire on cylinder 10 may be masked
c: Cylinder 10 sense lead shorted to a supply or adjacent ignition circuit
Poor ground at the evaluation side

P28B8.d: P28B8 is the general circuit code for ion sensing on cylinder 11: the evaluation electronics receive nothing usable from that cylinder, most often because the line from coil 11 is broken or its connector has lost contact. Eleven cylinders only occur on V12 and W12 engines, and none of them with ion sensing is publicly described; no manufacturer documents P28B8.
s: MIL on with a circuit fault stored for cylinder 11
Misfire and knock detection for cylinder 11 no longer available
Cautious ignition timing with slightly reduced power
c: Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin in the cylinder 11 coil connector
Broken ion signal wire between coil 11 and the evaluation module
Cylinder 11 input of the evaluation module damaged

P28B9.d: P28B9 stands for an ion signal from cylinder 11 whose voltage stays inside the valid band but whose behaviour makes no sense: too weak or too strong for the current speed and load, or out of line with the other eleven cylinders. Such rationality tests belong to the input-component monitoring CARB demands.
s: MIL on after the fault is confirmed on a second trip
Slightly rough running, sometimes with misfire code P0311
Unsteady ignition timing on cylinder 11
c: Worn or oil-fouled spark plug on cylinder 11
Cylinder 11 injector delivering too little or spraying poorly
Low compression on cylinder 11 (valve or ring leakage)
Water or oil standing in the plug well of cylinder 11

P28BA.d: P28BA means the cylinder 11 ion reading has fallen below its lower limit. Between sparks a bias voltage sits across the electrodes – 80 V on Saab's T7 – and burning gas lets a current flow that pulls this voltage down in proportion to pressure and temperature.
s: MIL on with a low ion signal stored for cylinder 11
Misfire code P0311 possible although the engine runs smoothly
Power slightly reduced by conservative timing
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 11 chafed and touching ground
Conductive deposits on the cylinder 11 plug insulator
Moisture or a carbon track in the cylinder 11 plug boot
Bias voltage generation in coil 11 failed

P28BB.d: P28BB is stored when the cylinder 11 ion signal remains above the highest value the measuring circuit can legitimately produce. Common reasons are a sense wire shorted to battery voltage or to another ignition circuit, an internal breakdown in coil 11 that couples spark energy into the measuring output, and a missing ground at the evaluator that lifts the whole reference.
s: Stored code for a high ion signal on cylinder 11, lamp behaviour depends on the maker
Real misfire on cylinder 11 may go undetected
Retarded timing on cylinder 11
c: Ion signal wire of cylinder 11 shorted to battery voltage or another ignition circuit
Internal breakdown in coil 11 feeding spark energy into the signal
Poor ground of the evaluation module shifting the reference

P28BC.d: P28BC covers a wiring-level failure in the ion measuring path of cylinder 12 that keeps a valid signal from arriving, typically an open wire or a connector without contact. Cylinder 12 is the last one on a V12 or W12; no such engine with ion sensing is publicly known, and no manufacturer documents P28BC.
s: MIL on with a circuit fault stored for cylinder 12
No combustion feedback from cylinder 12
Engine may run with reduced ignition advance
c: Open ion signal wire or connector at coil 12
Ignition trigger for cylinder 12 not reaching the detection module
Cylinder 12 channel of the evaluation module faulty

P28BD.d: P28BD reports that cylinder 12 delivers an ion signal of acceptable voltage whose content is not credible – its strength, timing or shape after the spark does not match the operating point or the rest of the engine. Saab's later detection module illustrates why content matters: it splits each raw ion trace with filters, a band-pass for the ringing that indicates knock and a low-pass for the slower part that describes
s: MIL on after the fault repeats on a later trip
Occasional roughness, sometimes with P0312
Knock control on cylinder 12 reacts erratically
c: Eroded or oil-wetted spark plug on cylinder 12
Mixture error on cylinder 12 (injector, intake leak at that port)
Carbon build-up in the cylinder 12 combustion chamber

P28BE.d: P28BE is set when the ion reading of cylinder 12 stays below its minimum. On Saab's Trionic T8 each coil generates its own measuring voltage of about 120 V and keeps it applied to the plug; the module then reads how much current the ionised gas lets through.
s: MIL on with a low ion signal stored for cylinder 12
Misfire code P0312 without noticeable roughness
Fault often appears after washing the engine or in wet weather
c: Water or oil in the cylinder 12 plug well draining the measuring voltage
Sense lead of cylinder 12 grounded against a bracket or the engine
Coil 12 no longer builds up its measuring voltage

P28BF.d: P28BF signals that the cylinder 12 ion input sits above its permitted window. A sense wire touching a powered conductor, moisture bridging pins in the coil 12 connector or spark energy escaping inside the coil can all push it there.
s: Stored high ion signal code for cylinder 12, MIL depending on the maker
Noticeably less power from heavy timing retard
Higher fuel consumption from protective enrichment
c: Sense wire of cylinder 12 touching a powered conductor
Moisture bridging pins in the coil 12 connector
Internal flashover in coil 12 reaching the measuring path

P28C0.d: P28C0 points to a fault in the power feed of the module that conditions ion signals – typically an open fuse, relay contact or wire, so the module is not powered at all. On Saab's Trionic T8 that module receives battery voltage via the main relay and its ground from a body point, and on the older T7 the ignition cassette took the same route.
s: Engine cranks but does not start, or cuts out while driving
Ion-based misfire and knock detection lost on all cylinders
Warning lamp behaviour depends on the manufacturer
c: Blown fuse in the ion sense module feed
Main relay not switching through or burnt contact
Open supply wire or loose ground point of the module
Internal fault in the module's power stage

P28C1.d: P28C1 means the ion sense module is powered, but its supply sits below the level it needs to work reliably. That matters because such modules turn 12 V into far higher voltages: Saab's T7 cassette converted battery voltage to 400 V DC stored in a capacitor and also kept 80 V across each plug for measuring.
s: Hard starting, especially when cold or with a weak battery
Misfire codes on several cylinders at once
Stored supply-voltage code, often together with system voltage codes
c: Voltage drop across a corroded main relay contact or connector
High-resistance ground point of the module

P28C2.d: P28C2 is stored when the voltage feeding the ion sense module exceeds its upper limit. Since the module derives its measuring and, in cassette designs, its ignition voltages from this feed, an excessive input can raise the bias across the plugs, push signals toward the top of their range and stress the converter inside.
s: Stored overvoltage code, often together with P0563
Flickering or unusually bright lamps, battery gassing
Erratic misfire or knock reports on several cylinders
c: Alternator voltage regulator letting the system voltage rise too high
Jump start or charger with excessive voltage (e.g. 24 V)
Poor module ground distorting the voltage reading
Faulty voltage measurement inside the module

P28C3.d: Under boost the intake manifold is above ambient pressure, so turbo engines add a high-load purge path: compressed air drives an ejector (venturi) that draws canister vapour into the compressor inlet, with check valves keeping boost out of the tank side. CARB requires every purge path to be checked for missing flow, from 2021 including disconnected lines, unless the high-load path carries under 1 percent of purge mas
s: MIL on, usually without any change in driving behaviour
EVAP readiness not completed
Occasional fuel smell after long full-load driving
c: Check valve in high-load line B sticking, leaking or fitted the wrong way round
Line B to the compressor inlet pulled off, cracked or kinked
Ejector nozzle blocked by debris or oil residue
Leak in the boost-side hose that drives the ejector

P28C4.d: P28C4 means the transmission controller finds the voltage too low on a phase lead (U, V or W) of the electric motor that operates clutch A. This layout belongs to wet dual-clutch gearboxes without a valve block, such as the Getrag/Magna 7DCT300 and its hybrid derivative 7HDT300: a brushless motor per clutch spins a gerotor pump that feeds oil directly to the clutch piston.
s: Transmission warning lamp, often together with the MIL
Odd or even gears locked out, depending on which shaft clutch A serves
Jerky or delayed pull-away
c: Phase wire to the clutch A motor chafed through and touching ground
Winding inside the clutch A motor shorted to the housing
Defective output transistor for the motor phases in the transmission controller

P28C5.d: With P28C5 the controller finds one or more phases of the clutch A motor sitting higher than the switching pattern allows, as if a lead were tied to battery voltage. The motor in question is the brushless drive of an on-demand pump actuator: Getrag introduced this concept with the 7DCT300, where one motor per clutch turns a gerotor pump and the pump pressure itself closes the clutch.
s: Warning lamp for the transmission and stored DTC
Half of the gear set unavailable, vehicle continues with reduced choice
Clutch A may not open or close on command
c: Motor phase lead shorted to a supply line in the harness
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins at the actuator connector
High-side switch in the controller that no longer turns off

P28C6.d: P28C6 is the general circuit code for the three-phase supply of the clutch A motor and is set above all when a phase carries no current although the controller drives it, i.e. an open line.
s: Clutch A does not engage, affected gears unavailable
Transmission warning and possibly MIL
Fault may come and go with vibration or temperature
c: Terminal pushed back or loose in the clutch A motor connector
Cracked solder joint or winding connection inside the actuator
Phase wire broken at a bend or bracket

P28C7.d: P28C7 flags that the clutch A motor's phases are electrically intact but the motor does not respond as expected, e.g. currents and rotation do not match the commanded drive.
s: MIL and transmission warning lamp on
Odd gears unavailable on the 7HDT300
Often stored together with clutch A temperature code P2787
c: Debris from the transmission jamming the pump in the clutch A actuator (Stellantis 7HDT300)
Worn or sluggish clutch A actuator motor
Increased resistance in a phase connection causing unbalanced currents

P28C8.d: P28C8 concerns the motor-and-pump unit of clutch A as a whole: the controller sees that the delivered result, typically the clutch pressure reported by the sensor or the motor effort needed to reach it, does not fit the command. In on-demand designs the gerotor pump is connected straight to the clutch cylinder, so pressure follows pump speed directly; a Hyundai-backed EVS32 study modelled exactly this arrangement and
s: Slipping or delayed engagement of clutch A
Transmission warning, gears on clutch A may be locked out
Audible whine from the actuator under load
c: Clutch A pump obstructed by abrasion particles
Internal leakage at the clutch A piston or pressure line seals
Low transmission fluid level so the pump draws air

P28C9.d: P28C9 is stored when the clutch A motor turns faster than the controller considers plausible for the pressure it is asked to hold. Because the pump in such actuators delivers oil straight into the closed clutch circuit, the motor should slow down once pressure is reached; if it keeps racing, the oil is escaping or the pump is not loaded.
s: Clutch A slips or fails to transmit full torque
Transmission warning and restricted gear choice
c: Oil escaping from the clutch A pressure circuit, e.g. worn piston seal
Pump drawing air because of low fluid level or clogged suction filter
Broken drive between motor shaft and gerotor rotor
Faulty motor position signal reporting too high a speed

P28CA.d: P28CA means the clutch A motor stays below the speed the controller commands, so the pump cannot deliver oil fast enough to build or modulate clutch pressure. Mechanical drag is the usual culprit: particles wedged in the gerotor, a seized bearing, or very thick oil in deep cold.
s: Clutch A engages late or with a jolt
Transmission warning, especially after cold start
Affected gears may be withheld
c: Particles jamming the gerotor pump of clutch A
Low supply voltage to the actuator or poor ground

P28CB.d: A brushless motor can only be commutated correctly if the electronics know where the rotor stands; P28CB reports that the signal from the sensor tracking the clutch A motor's rotor position is missing or electrically unusable, mostly through an open line. Without it the controller cannot switch the U-V-W phases in the right order or count motor revolutions, so the pump of clutch A is shut down.
s: Clutch A disabled, gears on that shaft unavailable
Transmission warning lamp
Possibly also motor speed codes stored
c: Open signal, supply or ground wire of the clutch A motor position sensor
Corroded or loose pin at the actuator connector
Failed position sensor inside the actuator

P28CC.d: P28CC is the plausibility counterpart to P28CB: the position signal of the clutch A motor arrives, but its values or their sequence make no sense, for example jumps between rotor angles, a missing step in the pattern, or a speed that contradicts the phase currents. CARB expects rationality checks of this kind for input components where feasible.
s: Clutch A engages roughly or intermittently
Transmission warning, sometimes only while driving
Gear changes on one shaft delayed or withheld
c: Electrical interference on the position signal through a damaged shield
Partly broken wire or loose contact causing signal dropouts
Loose sensor, shifted magnet or contaminated sensor target

P28CD.d: P28CD concerns the pressure sensor that tells the transmission controller how much oil pressure acts on clutch A. In pump-actuated wet DCTs there is no proportional valve to set pressure; instead Getrag places a pressure sensor downstream of the clutch pumps and closes the control loop over motor speed.
s: Clutch A shut off, half of the gears unavailable
Transmission warning lamp and stored code
c: Open signal, 5-volt supply or ground wire of the clutch A pressure sensor
Sensor connector not fully latched or pin pushed out
Internal open in the pressure sensor

P28CE.d: P28CE is logged when the clutch A pressure sensor output drops below the lowest voltage a working sensor can produce. Ratiometric pressure sensors are usually designed so that even zero pressure gives a small offset voltage; a reading underneath that band therefore means an electrical fault, not low pressure.
s: Clutch A disabled with transmission warning
Other sensor codes may be stored at the same time
Reduced choice of gears
c: Pressure sensor signal wire shorted to ground
5-volt reference pulled down by another sensor on the same supply
Internally shorted clutch A pressure sensor

P28CF.d: P28CF means the voltage from the clutch A pressure sensor climbs above the band a plausible measurement can reach, usually close to the reference or battery voltage. An open ground line is a frequent trigger, because many sensor circuits then float up to the supply level; a signal wire touching the 5-volt or 12-volt feed, or a sensor with a broken internal element, has the same effect.
s: Transmission warning, clutch A taken out of service
Pull-away or shifts only on the other clutch
c: Open ground wire of the clutch A pressure sensor
Signal wire shorted to the 5-volt reference or battery voltage
Pressure sensor failed with output stuck high

P28D0.d: P28D0 is the rationality fault of the clutch A pressure sensor: its voltage lies inside the valid window, but the indicated pressure does not match what the system should be producing. In a pump actuator the controller can cross-check this well, because pressure in the clutch circuit rises with pump motor speed and current; an EVS32 paper describes how directly the gerotor flow translates into clutch pressure.
s: Harsh or slipping engagement of clutch A
Transmission warning, possibly after some time driving
Gears on clutch A may be withheld
c: Clutch A pressure sensor drifting or sticking
Real pressure deviation from leakage or weak pump, misread as a sensor fault
Contact resistance in the signal path shifting the reading

P28D1.d: P28D1 is set when the power stage that drives the clutch A motor exceeds its current limit or its internal temperature limit. This output stage, usually part of the transmission controller or the actuator electronics, protects itself by shutting down or derating, after which clutch A can no longer be operated normally.
s: Transmission warning after heavy use, may clear after cooling down
Clutch A temporarily disabled
Possibly stored together with clutch temperature code P2787
c: Clutch A motor or pump hard to turn, e.g. jammed by particles
Long periods of high clutch pressure demand in stop-and-go or on gradients
Shorted motor winding drawing excess current

P28D2.d: P28D2 reports that on the U, V or W lead feeding the electric drive of clutch B a voltage below its expected level is measured, pointing to a short towards ground. Such motor-driven clutches are found in wet dual-clutch units of the Getrag/Magna pump-actuator family; the 7DCT300 went into series in 2015 with the Renault Espace, and the hybrid 7HDT300 uses the same principle.
s: Transmission warning light, MIL possible
Gears on the clutch B shaft unavailable (even gears on the 7HDT300)
Harsh or hesitant gear changes
c: Insulation of a clutch B motor phase rubbed through against ground
Water or corrosion in the clutch B actuator plug pulling a phase low
Failed low-side transistor of the clutch B motor driver

P28D3.d: P28D3 is the high-voltage fault on the phase wiring of the clutch B motor: a lead reads above what the inverter pattern should produce, typically because it contacts a positive feed or the upper switch cannot turn off. In the Getrag 7DCT300 five brushless motors share the housing, two for the shift drums, two for the clutch pumps and one for the cooling pump, so motor harnesses run close together and a chafed spot ca
s: Warning lamp and stored fault code
Vehicle drives on with only one clutch, gear choice reduced
Possible jerk when the controller drops clutch B
c: Clutch B motor phase touching a neighbouring positive feed in the harness
Corroded pins bridging at the clutch B motor connector
Upper output switch for the clutch B motor stays conducting

P28D4.d: P28D4 covers the circuit of the three motor phases for clutch B in general and is mainly logged when the controller energises a phase and no current returns, meaning the path is broken. Getrag chose brushless ferrite motors without rare earths for this pump-actuator generation and reused them from the 6DCT250; if one winding path is lost, the remaining two cannot turn the rotor smoothly, and the gerotor pump of clutc
s: Clutch B cannot be closed, its gears are blocked
Fault may appear only on rough roads or when hot
Transmission warning, MIL depending on make
c: Loose or spread crimp terminal on a clutch B motor phase
Phase wire fractured close to the clutch B actuator
Internal winding joint in the clutch B motor cracked by thermal cycling

P28D5.d: P28D5 means the clutch B motor wiring passes the electrical checks, yet the motor's behaviour, its phase currents and resulting rotation, does not follow what the controller demands. It is one of the few codes in this group with a public manufacturer reference: Stellantis bulletin 21-040-26 (May 2026), valid for Jeep Renegade and Compass of model years 2022-2025 sold in Europe with the 1.5 MHEV and the 7HDT300 hybrid
s: MIL on, transmission warning shown
Even gears not available on the 7HDT300
Often logged together with clutch B temperature code P27F3
c: Particles from the gearbox jamming a pump in the even-gear actuator (Stellantis 7HDT300)
Clutch B actuator motor running stiff or weak
Raised contact resistance on one phase causing uneven currents

P28D6.d: P28D6 tells that the electronic switch stage powering the clutch B motor has hit its overcurrent or overtemperature protection. Normally these pump actuators draw very little; Getrag quotes roughly 31 W (NEDC) and 33 W (WLTC) for the complete 7DCT300 actuation, so a stage running into its limits indicates the motor is working against unusual resistance or a fault in the stage itself.
s: Clutch B shut down temporarily, may recover after cooling
Transmission warning and restricted gears
May appear together with P27F3 or P28D5
c: Clutch B pump seized by particles, motor stalls and draws excess current
Turn-to-turn short in the clutch B motor winding
Prolonged high pressure demand with hot clutch, e.g. stop-and-go or towing
Defective output stage or poor heat transfer in the controller

P28D7.d: P28D7 judges motor and pump of clutch B as one unit: the oil pressure seen by the sensor, or the speed and current the motor needs for it, does not match the target. Getrag's hydraulic plan for the 7DCT300 has both clutch pumps drawing through a common suction filter, with a pressure sensor downstream of both pumps providing feedback.
s: Clutch B slips or engages late
Transmission warning, gears on clutch B possibly locked out
Unusual humming from the actuator area
c: Clogged common suction filter, especially if P28C8 is stored too
Leaking seals in the clutch B pressure circuit
Worn or contaminated gerotor set of the clutch B pump

P28D8.d: P28D8 sets when the clutch B motor spins faster than the controller expects for the commanded pressure. A gerotor works by positive displacement, the EVS32 model uses one with a seven-tooth outer rotor, so in a sealed clutch circuit its speed should fall once pressure is built; a motor that keeps accelerating means oil is escaping or the pump has lost its load.
s: Clutch B does not hold full torque, flaring on shifts
Transmission warning and limited gears
c: Worn piston or rotary feedthrough seal letting oil escape from the clutch B circuit
Aerated oil due to low level, pump runs without load
Sheared drive between clutch B motor shaft and inner rotor
Rotor position sensor reporting an excessive speed

P28D9.d: P28D9 indicates that the clutch B motor cannot reach the speed it is commanded to, leaving the pump short of flow to raise or adjust clutch pressure. Getrag states that its pump actuators control pressure consistently down to low temperatures, so a motor that persistently lags points to extra drag rather than normal cold behaviour: particles caught in the gerotor, a tight bearing, or oil of the wrong grade.
s: Delayed or jerky engagement of clutch B
Fault more likely after standing in the cold
Clutch B gears may be withheld
c: Particles caught in the clutch B gerotor pump
Tight or damaged bearing in the clutch B motor or pump
Incorrect transmission fluid with too high viscosity
Low supply voltage or poor ground at the actuator

P28DA.d: P28DA concerns the electrical circuit of the sensor that reports the rotor angle of the clutch B motor, and is chiefly stored when that signal disappears because a line is open. Electronic commutation of a brushless motor relies on this angle to energise U, V and W in the right order; it also lets the controller count revolutions and compare pump speed with the pressure sensor.
s: Clutch B out of service, half of the gears missing
Transmission warning lamp on
Motor speed codes for clutch B may be stored as follow-up faults
c: Open supply, ground or signal line of the clutch B motor position sensor
Pin pushed out or bent at the clutch B actuator connector
Failed sensing element inside the clutch B actuator

P28DB.d: P28DB flags a rotor position signal for the clutch B motor that is electrically present but fails the plausibility tests: angle steps arrive in a wrong order, a transition is skipped, or the derived speed disagrees with the phase currents and the measured clutch pressure. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 calls for such rationality monitoring of input signals where it is technically feasible, beyond pure circuit checks.
s: Clutch B engages roughly or drops out intermittently
Transmission warning, sometimes only after several trips
Motor speed codes for clutch B stored alongside
c: Electrical interference through a damaged screen on the sensor lead
Partly broken strand in the clutch B position sensor wiring
Sensor or target magnet shifted, or metallic debris on the target

P28DC.d: P28DC concerns the sensor that reports the hydraulic pressure acting on clutch B of a dual-clutch or hybrid transmission. The code points to a broken connection: the module receives no usable signal at all, as happens when a signal, supply or ground wire is open or the connector has come off.
s: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gears served by clutch B blocked, transmission in emergency mode
Jerky launch or harsh shifts
c: Connector at the sensor or transmission plug loose, unplugged or with a pushed-back pin
Signal, supply or ground wire of the sensor broken
Sensor input in the transmission control module faulty

P28DD.d: Set when the voltage from the clutch B pressure sensor falls below the lowest value the part can produce in normal service. Usually the signal line has a short to ground, the sensor supply is missing or the sensor has failed internally.
s: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Transmission in emergency mode, some gears unavailable
Harsh or delayed engagement
c: Sensor signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing or pulled down by another shorted sensor on the same supply

P28DE.d: P28DE means the clutch B pressure sensor delivers a voltage above anything a working sensor would show, even at full clutch pressure. Typical causes are a signal line touching a supply or battery feed, a broken sensor ground, or a signal line open at the sensor end where the input uses a pull-up resistor.
s: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Emergency mode with limited gears
Slipping or weak pull when clutch B is in use
c: Signal wire shorted to the sensor supply or to battery voltage
Sensor ground open or high resistance at the connector
Pressure sensor failed with output stuck high

P28DF.d: Here the clutch B pressure signal is electrically valid, yet it does not fit the situation. Examples are a reading that stays well above zero while the clutch is released, a value that does not rise when the actuator builds pressure, or a mismatch between commanded and measured pressure that persists.
s: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Shudder, slip or jerky engagement on clutch B
Emergency mode after a few drives
c: Pressure sensor drifting or with offset at zero pressure
Actual clutch pressure wrong because of leaking seals, a weak actuator pump or low fluid
Corroded or loose contacts distorting the signal
Control software needs an update or new adaptation

P28E0.d: The shift motor is the three-phase electric motor of an electronic range actuator: in shift-by-wire systems it turns the detent plate and selector shaft between P, R, N and D. A Denso patent describes such a motor whose driver energises the U, V and W phases in turn, with a motor relay in the supply; Hyundai Kefico sells its SBW actuator with a brushless motor.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Selected range cannot be changed, vehicle may stay in Park
Engine may not start because Park or Neutral is not confirmed
c: Phase lead to the actuator chafed and shorted to ground
Motor winding shorted to the actuator housing (moisture, insulation damage)
Output stage in the shift control unit faulty

P28E1.d: P28E1 is the opposite of P28E0: on any of the three shift motor phases the controller sees a voltage that is higher than the switching state allows, for example while the low-side switch should pull it down. Likely reasons are a phase lead touching a battery-powered wire, a winding with an internal short to a live part, or a high-side switch in the driver that no longer turns off.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
No response to the gear selector
Vehicle may remain in Park
c: Phase lead shorted to a battery-voltage wire in the harness
High-side switch in the shift control unit stuck on
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the actuator connector

P28E2.d: P28E2 reports that no current can flow in at least one shift motor phase, usually a broken lead, a loose terminal or an open winding. Hyundai documents it in bulletin 22-AT-001H with failure type 14 (P28E214), an open UVW motor circuit, for the push-button shift-by-wire of the 2020-on Palisade and Sonata, the 2021-on Santa Fe and Santa Fe Hybrid and the 2022-on Tucson and Tucson Hybrid.
s: Shifter system malfunction message in the cluster
Cannot shift into or out of gear or out of Park
Wrong gear display or no start
c: Actuator harness chafed open, on the Santa Fe at the battery tray (Hyundai 22-AT-001H)
Loose or damaged pin in the SBW actuator connector
Open winding inside the SBW actuator

P28E3.d: P28E3 covers the phase circuits of the shift motor when none of them is clearly open or shorted, yet they do not behave as expected: one phase draws noticeably more or less current than the others, or the current pattern does not match the commutation step. Such an imbalance comes from a phase with raised resistance, a partly shorted winding or a weak switch in the driver, and it shows up as uneven torque.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Slow or noisy range changes
Occasional refusal to change range
c: Corroded or loose contact raising the resistance of one phase
Partly shorted turns in a motor winding
Degraded switch in the motor driver

P28E4.d: P28E4 says the output stage that powers the shift motor has reached its current or temperature limit and has protected itself. A blocked actuator is the classic trigger: if the detent plate, the park pawl linkage or the gear train inside the actuator binds, the motor stalls and current climbs.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Range change stops halfway or is refused
Problem may disappear after the system cools down
c: Detent mechanism, park pawl linkage or actuator gearing binding
Driver overheated after repeated range changes or high ambient heat

P28E5.d: P28E5 judges the shift motor by its result: it is driven, but the actuator does not get to the commanded range as expected. Hyundai lists it in bulletin 22-AT-001H for the shift-by-wire Palisade, Santa Fe, Sonata and Tucson (including hybrids) with two failure types: P28E577, commanded position not reached, and P28E592, SBW motor performance.
s: Shifter system malfunction message in the cluster
Range not engaged or engaged with delay
Wrong gear display
c: SBW actuator worn internally or mechanism stiff
Shift control unit or its harness not delivering motor current
Low 12 V supply during the shift
Shift control software needing an update

P28E6.d: P28E6 is set when the shift motor turns faster than its control allows. In a position-controlled actuator this is visible from the rotor feedback: the encoder count changes quicker than the commanded movement can explain.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Wrong range engaged or range change aborted
Clicking or whirring from the actuator
c: Broken gear or coupling inside the actuator, motor spins without load
Faulty rotor position or encoder signal
Control software error in the shift control unit

P28E7.d: The shift motor position sensor tells the controller where the selector shaft of a shift-by-wire actuator stands. In a Denso patent it is a contactless magnetic sensor on the detent plate with two independent units, so two signals reach the ECU; Hyundai notes in bulletin 22-AT-001H that the readings of its two position sensors should add up to roughly 100 percent.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Gear display missing or wrong
Vehicle refuses to shift or does not start
c: Position sensor connector loose, corroded or unplugged
Signal, supply or ground wire of the sensor broken

P28E8.d: P28E8 means the shift motor position sensor reports a value above its permitted range. Kia documents it on the 2024-25 EV9: service action SA594 (bulletin ELE362, January 2025) covers cars built from 25 September 2023 to 4 September 2024 that may not leave Park while P28E812 is stored, which Kia attributes to an output shaft sensor reading above what it should be.
s: Vehicle cannot be shifted out of Park
Shift system warning in the cluster
c: Shift control unit software on the 2024-25 Kia EV9 (service action SA594)
Sensor signal shorted to supply or battery voltage
Position sensor failed with output stuck high

P28E9.d: P28E9 is stored when the signal of the shift motor position sensor sits below its valid band. Typical causes are a signal line shorted to ground, a sensor supply that has collapsed, for instance because another sensor on the same feed is shorted, or a failed sensor.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Range changes blocked or gear display wrong
Engine or drive system may not start
c: Sensor signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply missing or pulled down
Position sensor failed with output stuck low

P28EA.d: P28EA covers a position signal that is electrically valid but implausible: the two channels disagree, the value does not move although the motor runs, or the actuator ends up away from the expected detent. Hyundai uses the code in bulletin 22-AT-001H for its shift-by-wire models with two failure types, P28EA71, SBW actuator stuck, and P28EA77, commanded position not reached.
s: Shifter system malfunction message in the cluster
Cannot shift out of Park or into the requested range
Gear display does not match the selected range
c: SBW actuator stuck or not reaching the commanded position
Position sensor channels drifting apart (sum no longer near 100 percent)
Intermittent contact in the sensor or actuator harness

P28EB.d: A shift-by-wire actuator has to learn which motor positions match P, R, N and D before it can work precisely. A Hyundai Autron patent does this from motor current: while the actuator travels between P and D, the load changes each time the detent spring passes one of the four notches of the detent plate, so R and N are found first and P and D derived by offset.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Imprecise or refused range changes until learning is done
c: Learning routine not run after replacing the control unit or actuator
Learned values cleared by a software update or memory loss
Learning aborted by low battery voltage or an active fault

P28EC.d: Unlike P28EB, learning did take place here, but the result lies outside the window the controller accepts. The learned sensor values for the end stop or for the P, R, N and D detents differ too far from the nominal ones, or the measured play is too large.
s: Shift system warning in the cluster
Learning routine fails repeatedly
Range changes imprecise or blocked
c: Actuator or sensor mounted out of position after a repair
Worn or damaged detent plate, detent spring or linkage
Wrong or mismatched actuator or sensor fitted

P28ED.d: Pump B is a second electrically driven transmission fluid pump that works independently of the engine, for example to hold pressure during start-stop or electric driving, or to feed clutch cooling. P28ED says its motor runs faster than commanded or faster than its permitted maximum.
s: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Start-stop or electric driving disabled
Whining from the pump area
c: Low fluid level or air drawn in, so the pump runs without load
Faulty speed feedback or control in the pump controller

P28EE.d: P28EE is the reverse of P28ED: electric transmission fluid pump B does not reach the speed its controller asks for. The motor is fed, but something holds it back, such as very cold and thick fluid, a binding or worn pump, debris in the gears or a low supply voltage.
s: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Engine keeps running at stops, electric driving limited
Delayed engagement after an automatic engine restart
c: Pump binding, worn or contaminated with debris
Very cold, aged or wrong transmission fluid
Low supply voltage or high resistance in the pump feed

P28EF.d: In a P2 hybrid a clutch placed between combustion engine and e-machine lets the car drive electrically with the engine at rest and couples the engine back in when it is needed. P28EF says the device that applies this clutch is not doing its job: it is commanded to act, but the expected pressure or clutch response stays absent, so the actuator behaves as if switched off.
s: Engine does not start or does not engage while driving in hybrid mode
Gearbox or hybrid system warning in the cluster
Reduced power or electric-only limp mode
c: Pressure regulating valve of the disconnect clutch sticking or mechanically faulty
Contaminated or low transmission fluid, so the actuator cannot build pressure
Electric or mechanical oil pump delivers too little pressure to the clutch circuit
Control software or learned clutch values out of date

P28F0.d: P28F0 is the opposite of P28EF: the actuator of the engine disconnect clutch keeps applying the clutch although the controller wants it released. The engine then stays tied to e-machine and wheels, so electric-only driving and engine stop at standstill are no longer possible.
s: Engine stalls or shudders when the car comes to a stop
No electric-only driving, engine runs all the time
Hybrid system warning and restricted engine restarts
c: Clutch pressure valve stuck in the applied position, for example by debris
Valve or actuator driver permanently energised by a short in wiring or module
Clutch plates overheated and dragging so the actuator cannot release them

P28F1.d: A hydraulically applied disconnect clutch often has its own pressure sensor so the controller knows how firmly the clutch is held. Ford fits one to the 10R80 modular hybrid transmission of the 2021 Explorer, Aviator and F-150 hybrids; a Ford bulletin covers fluid seeping out at this sensor because its fasteners worked loose, fixed by retightening them.
s: Hybrid or transmission warning light
Engine stays off or engages harshly when it should join in
Possible fluid wetness around the sensor
c: Sensor connector loose, corroded or with a pushed-back terminal
Signal, reference or ground wire of the sensor broken
Pressure sensor electronics failed, possibly after fluid ingress at a leaking seal
Sensor input of the transmission or hybrid control module faulty

P28F2.d: Here the wiring is intact and the voltage lies inside the valid band, yet the reading does not fit the situation. A Hyundai and Kia patent describes one such test: when the car is parked, the electric oil pump for the engine clutch is off, a soak time has passed and the vehicle stands still, no pressure can exist, so a sensor output above a set reference counts as a fault.
s: Clutch slips or engages abruptly when the engine is coupled in
Hybrid or transmission warning light
Shudder during engine start while driving electrically
c: Pressure sensor zero point drifted or wrongly learned
Real residual pressure from a sticking valve, so the sensor is not at fault
High resistance in sensor ground or signal line shifting the reading

P28F3.d: P28F3 is stored when the voltage of the disconnect clutch pressure sensor drops below the smallest value a healthy part can output, a level that stands for an electrical fault, not for an open clutch. The usual suspects are a signal wire chafed against ground, a sensor reference supply that is missing or dragged down by another shorted sensor on the same feed, or a failed sensor.
s: Hybrid or transmission warning light
Engine coupling blocked, car runs electrically or in limp mode
Harsh engagement if the clutch is still used
c: Signal wire shorted to ground through chafed insulation
Sensor reference supply missing or pulled low by another shorted sensor
Pressure sensor failed with output stuck low

P28F4.d: With P28F4 the disconnect clutch pressure sensor sends a voltage above anything it could produce even at full clutch pressure. Typical reasons are a signal line touching the reference or battery supply, an open sensor ground, or on inputs with a pull-up resistor a signal wire that is broken at the sensor.
s: Hybrid or transmission warning light
Clutch slips when the engine is meant to drive
Electric-only operation or reduced power
c: Signal wire shorted to sensor reference or battery voltage
Sensor ground open or corroded at the connector
Pressure sensor failed with output stuck high

P28F5.d: P28F5 covers a pressure signal from the engine disconnect clutch that jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than the hydraulics physically allow. Each sample may sit inside the valid band, but the pattern points to a loose contact, a wire that breaks under vibration or heat, or an unstable sensor.
s: Hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional jerk when the engine is coupled in
Fluid seepage at the sensor in some cases
c: Loose or corroded terminal in the sensor or transmission connector
Harness wire breaking intermittently under vibration or heat
Sensor loose on its mounting or internally unstable

P28F6.d: P28F6 points at the electrical side of the disconnect clutch actuator rather than at its mechanics: the drive circuit to the valve or motor that applies the clutch loses or regains its normal state for short moments, typically spotted as current or feedback that flickers between plausible and implausible. Loose pins, a harness rubbing through under engine movement and connectors with fluid inside are the usual culpri
s: Sporadic hybrid or transmission warning
Engine occasionally fails to couple in or drops out
Jerks or brief power loss in hybrid mode
c: Loose, spread or corroded terminal in the actuator circuit
Harness chafing intermittently against the transmission or body
Transmission fluid wicking into the connector
Actuator coil or motor winding with an intermittent break

P28F7.d: P28F7 reports that the pressure in the exhaust of bank 1 is higher than the engine model allows. GM documents it in its 2025 diesel ECM tables (25OBDG04B): the monitor looks at the low-pressure EGR differential pressure and fails above 80 kPa while torque demand exceeds a speed-dependent minimum (around 520 Nm at low engine speed, falling to 20 Nm at high speed), counting 480 failures in 600 samples; it is Type A, MI
s: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power
Higher fuel consumption and more frequent filter regenerations
c: Exhaust throttle valve stuck closed or its shaft linkage broken
Exhaust restricted downstream, for example by a heavily loaded particulate filter or damaged pipe
Chafed engine harness disturbing valve control (GM 21-NA-149)
Pressure sensor reading too high without a separate sensor code

P28F8.d: P28F8 is the bank 2 twin of P28F7 and only appears on engines whose two cylinder banks have separately measured exhaust paths, such as V engines with one turbocharger or flap per bank. It means the exhaust pressure on that side exceeds the modelled value.
s: Check engine light on
Loss of power, possibly with uneven running between banks
Increased fuel consumption
c: Exhaust flap or throttle on bank 2 stuck closed
Restriction downstream on bank 2, for example a blocked catalyst or filter section
Variable turbine of the bank 2 turbocharger stuck in a closed position

P28F9.d: P28F9 flags exhaust pressure on bank 1 that stays below what the engine should produce at the current load. Too little pressure ahead of the turbine means the gas is escaping or not being held back: a leak at the manifold, gasket or turbine inlet, an exhaust flap jammed open, or a variable turbine stuck wide open.
s: Check engine light on
Weak boost and sluggish acceleration
Ticking or hissing exhaust noise near the manifold
c: Exhaust leak at manifold, gasket or turbine inlet on bank 1
Variable turbine geometry stuck in the open position
Exhaust throttle or pressure flap jammed open
Leaking or cracked sensing tube to the exhaust pressure sensor

P28FA.d: P28FA is the bank 2 version of P28F9: the exhaust on the second cylinder bank carries less pressure than the load calls for. It presupposes an engine with a separate pressure reading per bank, such as a V engine with one turbocharger on each side.
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power and slow boost build-up
Exhaust noise or soot traces on bank 2
c: Cracked manifold or leaking gasket on bank 2
Bank 2 turbocharger vanes or wastegate stuck open
Exhaust pressure flap of bank 2 jammed open
